extraction_notes.note: Equations \eqref{key2} and \eqref{key3} are empty numbered equation environments (the displays follow as $$...$$), so they get no node and the \eqref references to them resolve to nothing.
The labels operator_far and sup_displaced are each used twice in the source, so \eqref references to them are ambiguous; the finishing step attaches them to one of the two equations.

Equation (1.10) restates (3.21) of Theorem 3.1 and the unnumbered-in-text phase display in Section 3.3 restates (3.10); both are restated copies and get no node. The informal bullets of Section 1.3, the 'Philosophy'/'Main strategy' outline and Figure 1 are road-map prose and were not extracted.

Footnotes extending the main theorem to curves $\gamma+C$ and the trivial point $C=(\infty,\infty,\infty)$, the reduction to $m=n$ and $t>0$ in Section 3.3, and the discarding of $R_j$ as an error term were left in prose without nodes.
The paper's 'Observation' environments were typed by content: those asserting something used later or argued (1.2, 3.6, 3.7, 5.4) as claim, Observation 4.8 (a methodological aside) as remark.

Theorem 4.4's two items are proved in separate subsubsections, so each item is a nested claim that receives its proof; Theorem 4.4 itself has no proof node and Theorems 4.2-4.3 are derived from it by a prose proof.
The open problem is a footnote sentence inside the Lacey-Thiele sentence; it starts after \footnote{, which the boundary check flags as mid-sentence.

Lemma 3.3(i) is attributed to Lie 2018 (Lemma 4.8) while (ii) and Lemma 3.4 are new but unproved ('similar techniques'); the lemmas are kept whole as origin paper with rigor semi_formal rather than split.
The main theorem and Theorem 3.5 have no proof environment: their proofs are assembled across Sections 3-5; this is recorded by uses edges from the component theorems and claims.

nodes.name: Bilinear maximal function along a curve
nodes.statement: That is, given $\Gamma=(t,-\gamma(t))$ where $\gamma$ is a suitable smooth, non-flat curve near zero and near infinity, we ask about the boundedness properties of the bilinear maximal function along $\Gamma$ defined by \begin{align} M_\Gamma&:\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R})\times\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R})\to L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}) \nonumber\\ M_\Gamma(f,g)(x)&:=\sup\limits_{\varepsilon>0} \frac{1}{2\varepsilon} \int_{-\varepsilon}^\varepsilon |f(x-t)g(x+\gamma(t))|dt. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Defines $M_\Gamma(f,g)(x)=\sup_\varepsilon \frac{1}{2\varepsilon}\int_{-\varepsilon}^{\varepsilon}|f(x-t)g(x+\gamma(t))|dt$ for $\Gamma=(t,-\gamma(t))$.

nodes.name: Definition of $M_\Gamma$
nodes.statement: M_\Gamma&:\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R})\times\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R})\to L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}) \nonumber\\ M_\Gamma(f,g)(x)&:=\sup\limits_{\varepsilon>0} \frac{1}{2\varepsilon} \int_{-\varepsilon}^\varepsilon |f(x-t)g(x+\gamma(t))|dt.
nodes.label: definition

nodes.name: Bilinear Hilbert transform along $\Gamma$
nodes.statement: H_{\Gamma}(f,g)(x):= \textrm{p.v.}\int_{\mathbb{R}} f(x-t)\,g(x+\gamma(t))\frac{dt}{t}
nodes.label: nhilb

nodes.name: Lacey-Thiele bounds for the bilinear Hilbert transform
nodes.statement: This was approached by M. Lacey and C. Thiele in \cite{lt1} and \cite{lt2} where they proved that $H_{\Gamma}$ obeys $L^p\times L^q \to L^r$ bounds\footnote{It is still an open problem if this range is optimal.} for $\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}=\frac{1}{r}$ with $1<p,\,q\leq \infty$ and $\frac{2}{3}<r<\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: In the flat case the bilinear Hilbert transform is bounded $L^p\times L^q\to L^r$ for Hoelder indices with $1<p,q\le\infty$, $2/3<r<\infty$.

nodes.name: Optimality of the Lacey-Thiele range
nodes.statement: It is still an open problem if this range is optimal.
nodes.statement_short: Whether the range $2/3<r<\infty$ for the flat bilinear Hilbert transform is optimal is open.

nodes.name: Lacey's bilinear maximal function theorem
nodes.statement: The analogous result for the operator $M_{\Gamma}$ was proved by Lacey in \cite{la3}.

nodes.name: Li's $L^2\times L^2\to L^1$ bound for the bilinear Hilbert transform along $(t,t^d)$
nodes.statement: in the nonzero-curvature (or non-flat) case, \emph{e.g.} when $\gamma''$ is nonzero near origin and infinity, the problem of providing bounds for $H_{\Gamma}$ was first addressed by X. Li (\cite{li}), in the special case $\Gamma(t) = (t, t^d)$, $2 \leq d \in \mathbb N$, by proving that $H_{\Gamma}$ obeys $L^{2}\times L^{2} \to L^{1}$ bounds.

nodes.name: Boundedness of the bilinear Hilbert transform along non-flat curves
nodes.statement: In \cite{lie2015boundedness} and \cite{lie2015triangle} the second author of the present paper proved the maximal range up to end-points for $H_{\Gamma}$ where here $\gamma$ belongs to a suitable class of curves $\mathcal{N}\mathcal{F}$ that includes in particular any generalized (Laurent) real polynomial with no linear term.\footnote{\emph{I.e.}, any expression of the form $\gamma(t):=\sum_{j=1}^d a_j t^{\alpha_j}$ with $\{a_j\}_{j=1}^{d}\subset\mathbb{R}$, $\{\alpha_j\}_{j=1}^{d}\subset\mathbb{R}\setminus\{1\}$ and $d\in\mathbb{N}$. Here, we use the following convention: if $\alpha,\,t\in \mathbb{R}$ we let $t^{\alpha}$ stand for either $|t|^{\alpha}$ or $\textrm{sgn}\, (t)\, |t|^{\alpha}$. In a follow up paper, \cite{AG}, the first author extends the present result (and its singular integral analogue in \cite{lie2015boundedness} and \cite{lie2015triangle}) to the case in which one allows the curve $\gamma$ to be a generalized polynomial but with the linear term included.}
nodes.statement_short: For curves in the class $\mathcal{NF}$, $H_\Gamma$ is bounded in the maximal range up to end-points.

nodes.name: Li-Xiao uniform estimates for polynomial curves
nodes.statement: Later, elaborating on the ideas and techniques in both \cite{li} and \cite{lie2015boundedness}, the authors in \cite{liXiao2016uniform} prove for both $H_{\Gamma}$ and $M_{\Gamma}$ the expected H\"older range in the case $\gamma(t)$ a standard polynomial with no linear term with bounds that are uniform in the polynomial's coefficients.
nodes.statement_short: For polynomial curves without linear term, $H_\Gamma$ and $M_\Gamma$ obey the expected Hoelder range with coefficient-uniform bounds.

nodes.name: Class $\mathcal{NF}$ of non-flat curves
nodes.statement: In what follows, we refer to \cite[Section 2]{lie2015boundedness} for the definition of the class $\mathcal{NF}$ of smooth ``non-flat'' curves near zero and infinity.
differentia: smooth ``non-flat'' curves near zero and infinity

nodes.name: Main Theorem: boundedness of the bilinear maximal function along non-flat curves
nodes.statement: Let $\Gamma=(t,-\gamma(t))$ be a curve such that\footnote{It is easy to notice that our main result extends to the class of curves $\mathcal{NF}^{C}$ that is defined to be the set of all curves $\gamma\,+\,C$ with $\gamma\in\mathcal{NF}$ and $C\in\mathbb{R}$, \textit{i.e.}, our result is closed under translation by constants of $\gamma$ with $\gamma\in\mathcal{NF}$.} $\gamma\in\mathcal{NF}$. Consider the bilinear maximal function defined by \eqref{definition}. Then $M_\Gamma$ extends boundedly from $L^p(\mathbb{R})\times L^{q}(\mathbb{R})$ into $L^r(\mathbb{R})$ where the indices $p, q, r$ obey \begin{equation} \frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}=\frac{1}{r}, \end{equation} and\footnote{Observe that one gets trivially the desired bound for the triple of indices $(p,q,r)=(\infty,\infty,\infty)$ corresponding to the point $C$ in Figure \ref{triangle_fig}. That is why we will exclude this case from all our future reasonings.} \begin{equation} 1<p\leq\infty\,,\, 1<q\leq\infty \mbox{ and } 1\leq r\leq \infty. \end{equation} This result is sharp.
assumptions: Consider the bilinear maximal function defined by \eqref{definition}.
conclusions: Then $M_\Gamma$ extends boundedly from $L^p(\mathbb{R})\times L^{q}(\mathbb{R})$ into $L^r(\mathbb{R})$ where the indices $p, q, r$ obey
nodes.statement_short: For $\gamma\in\mathcal{NF}$, $M_\Gamma$ is bounded $L^p\times L^q\to L^r$ for all Hoelder triples with $1<p,q\le\infty$, $1\le r\le\infty$, and this range is sharp.
nodes.label: main_theorem

nodes.name: Hoelder relation $1/p+1/q=1/r$
nodes.statement: \frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}=\frac{1}{r},
nodes.label: exponents10

nodes.name: Range of exponents $1<p,q\le\infty$, $1\le r\le\infty$
nodes.statement: 1<p\leq\infty\,,\, 1<q\leq\infty \mbox{ and } 1\leq r\leq \infty.
nodes.label: exponents20

nodes.name: Observation 1.2: sharpness of the range $r\ge1$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{P}_d$ be the class of all real polynomials of degree $d$ with no linear and constant terms. In \cite[Section 3]{liXiao2016uniform}, the authors show that for any $d\in\mathbb{N}$, $d\ge2$, there exists a polynomial $P_d\in\mathcal{P}_d$ such that for $\Gamma=(t,P(t))$ one has that $M_\Gamma$ is unbounded whenever $p, q, r$ obey \eqref{exponents10} with $1<p, q<\infty$ and $r<\frac{d-1}{d}$. However, for any $d\in\mathbb{N}$, $d\ge2$ we have that $\mathcal{P}_d\subset\mathcal{NF}$. Thus, in order for \eqref{exponents10} and \eqref{exponents20} to hold for any $\gamma\in\mathcal{NF}$ we must have $r\ge 1$, hence the claimed optimality of the range in our theorem above.
nodes.statement_short: Li-Xiao polynomial counterexamples, which lie in $\mathcal{NF}$, force $r\ge1$, so the range of the main theorem is optimal.

nodes.name: Li-Xiao unboundedness for polynomial curves below $r=(d-1)/d$
nodes.statement: In \cite[Section 3]{liXiao2016uniform}, the authors show that for any $d\in\mathbb{N}$, $d\ge2$, there exists a polynomial $P_d\in\mathcal{P}_d$ such that for $\Gamma=(t,P(t))$ one has that $M_\Gamma$ is unbounded whenever $p, q, r$ obey \eqref{exponents10} with $1<p, q<\infty$ and $r<\frac{d-1}{d}$.
nodes.statement_short: For each $d\ge2$ some polynomial curve of degree $d$ makes $M_\Gamma$ unbounded when $r<(d-1)/d$.

nodes.name: Dyadic decomposition $H_\Gamma=\sum_j H_j$
nodes.statement: H_{\Gamma}(f,g)=\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}} H_j(f,g):=\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}} \int_{\mathbb{R}} f(x-t)\,g(x+\gamma(t)) \rho_j(t)\,dt\,,
nodes.label: hilg

nodes.name: Mean zero condition $\int\rho=0$
nodes.statement: \int_{\mathbb{R}}\rho(t)dt=0\,.
nodes.label: mzh

nodes.name: Dyadic representation $M_\Gamma=\sup_j M_j$
nodes.statement: M_{\Gamma}(f,g)=\sup_{j\in\mathbb{Z}} M_j(f,g):=\sup_{j\in\mathbb{Z}} \int_{\mathbb{R}} f(x-t)\,g(x+\gamma(t))\underline{\rho}_j(t)\,dt\,,
nodes.label: mg

nodes.name: Normalization $\int\underline{\rho}=1$
nodes.statement: \int_{\mathbb{R}}\underline{\rho}(t)dt=1\,.
nodes.label: nzh

nodes.name: Remark 1: $l^1$-sum versus $l^\infty$-sum
nodes.statement: \noindent \textsf{Remark 1} \emph{Thus, in a nutshell, one has \begin{itemize} \item $H_{\Gamma}$ is a conditional $l^1$-sum of pieces $\{H_j\}_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}$ with the associated kernels $\{\rho_j\}$ having mean zero; \item $M_{\Gamma}$ is an $l^{\infty}$-sum of pieces $\{M_j\}_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}$ with the associated kernels $\{\underline{\rho}_j\}$ integrating to one. \end{itemize}}
nodes.statement_short: $H_\Gamma$ is a conditional $l^1$-sum of mean-zero pieces $H_j$, while $M_\Gamma$ is an $l^\infty$-sum of pieces $M_j$ with kernels integrating to one.

nodes.name: Three-part decomposition $M_j=M_j^L+M_j^{H\not\Delta}+M_j^{H\Delta}$
nodes.statement: M_j=M_j^L+M_j^{H\not\Delta}+M_j^{H\Delta}\,,
nodes.label: multiplierM

nodes.name: Remark 2: only the low frequency component sees the mean zero condition
nodes.statement_short: Only the low-frequency components distinguish $M_j$ from $H_j$; the high-frequency components can be identified with their Hilbert analogues.

nodes.name: Decomposition of the main term in $m$
nodes.statement: M_{j(x)}^{H\Delta}(f,g)(x)=\sum_{m\in\mathbb{N}} M_{j(x),m}^{H\Delta}(f,g)(x)\,,
nodes.label: decm

nodes.name: Single-scale $L^2\times L^2\to L^1$ decay for $M^{H\Delta}_{j,m}$
nodes.statement: \|M^{H\Delta}_{j,m}(f,g)\|_{L^1}\lesssim_{\gamma} 2^{-\epsilon m}\|f\|_2\,\|g\|_{2}.
nodes.label: l2cs

nodes.name: Variable-scale $L^2\times L^2\to L^1$ decay for $M^{H\Delta}_{j(x),m}$
nodes.statement: \|M^{H\Delta}_{j(x),m}(f,g)(x)\|_{L^1(dx)}\leq \sum_{j} \|M^{H\Delta}_{j,m}(f,g)\|_{L^1}\lesssim_{\gamma} 2^{-\epsilon m}\|f\|_2\,\|g\|_{2}\,,
nodes.label: l2css

nodes.name: Non-negative inputs
nodes.statement: Without lost of generality, from now on throughout the paper, we will assume that $f$ and $g$ are non-negative functions.

nodes.name: Dilation, moment and derivative notation for $\phi$
nodes.statement: For example, given any $\phi\in\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R})$, $j,\,l\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $k\in\mathbb{N}$, we set \begin{align} \phi_j(x)&:=\phi\big(\frac{x}{2^j}\big),\\ \tilde\phi_{l}(x)&:=x^l\phi(x),\\ \phi^{(k)}(x)&:=\left(\frac{d}{dx}\right)^k\phi(x),\\ \tilde\phi_{l,j}(x)&:=\tilde\phi_l\big(\frac{x}{2^j}\big). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Notation $\phi_j$, $\tilde\phi_l=x^l\phi$, $\phi^{(k)}$ and $\tilde\phi_{l,j}$ for a Schwartz function $\phi$.

nodes.name: Notation $\phi_j$, $\tilde\phi_l$, $\phi^{(k)}$, $\tilde\phi_{l,j}$
nodes.statement: \phi_j(x)&:=\phi\big(\frac{x}{2^j}\big),\\ \tilde\phi_{l}(x)&:=x^l\phi(x),\\ \phi^{(k)}(x)&:=\left(\frac{d}{dx}\right)^k\phi(x),\\ \tilde\phi_{l,j}(x)&:=\tilde\phi_l\big(\frac{x}{2^j}\big).
nodes.label: notation2

nodes.name: Fourier transform and inverse Fourier transform
nodes.statement: If $f\in \mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R})$ we denote the Fourier transform of $f$ with $\hat{f}$, where\footnote{In our later reasonings we will often ignore the constant $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}$.} $$\hat{f}(\xi):=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_{\mathbb{R}} f(x)\,e^{-i x \xi}\,d x\,,\:\:\:\:\:\:\xi\in\mathbb{R}\,$$ and the inverse Fourier transform of $f$ with $\check{f}$, where $$\check{f}(\xi):=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_{\mathbb{R}} f(x)\,e^{i x \xi}\,d x\,,\:\:\:\:\:\:\xi\in\mathbb{R}\,.$$

nodes.name: Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator
nodes.statement: We denote by $M$ the standard Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator defined on $L^1_\text{loc}(\mathbb{R})$ as \[Mf(x):=\sup\limits_{\substack{I\ni x\\ I\text{ interval}}}\frac{1}{|I|}\int_I |f(x)|dx.\]

nodes.name: $t$-shifted square function and $t$-shifted maximal function
nodes.statement: For $t\in\mathbb{R}$ and $\varphi\in C^\infty_0$ with $\varphi(0)=0$ we define the $t$-\emph{shifted square functions} with respect to $\varphi$ by \begin{equation} S_t^{\varphi}f(x):=\Big(\sum\limits_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\Big|(f* (2^j\check{\varphi}(2^j\cdot)))\big(x-\frac{t}{2^j} \big)\Big|^2\Big)^\frac{1}{2}\,, \end{equation} and the $t$-\emph{shifted maximal function} by\footnote{As expected, in the maximal function case, the mean zero condition of $\varphi$ becomes irrelevant and one can replace the original conditions imposed on $\varphi$ by merely $\check{\varphi}\in \mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R})$ any (normalized) function with $\check{\varphi}\geq 0$ and $\|\check{\varphi}\|_{L^1(\mathbb{R})}=1$. Given this, in what follows we no longer specify the dependence of our maximal function on $\varphi$.} \begin{equation} M^{(t)}f(x):=\sup\limits_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\Big|(f* (2^j\check{\varphi}(2^j\cdot)))\big(x-\frac{t}{2^j} \big)\Big|\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $S_t^\varphi f$ is the Littlewood-Paley square function with the $j$-th piece shifted by $t2^{-j}$; $M^{(t)}f$ is the analogous shifted maximal function.

nodes.name: $t$-shifted square function $S_t^{\varphi}$
nodes.statement: S_t^{\varphi}f(x):=\Big(\sum\limits_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\Big|(f* (2^j\check{\varphi}(2^j\cdot)))\big(x-\frac{t}{2^j} \big)\Big|^2\Big)^\frac{1}{2}\,,
nodes.label: shif_max

nodes.name: $t$-shifted maximal function $M^{(t)}$
nodes.statement: M^{(t)}f(x):=\sup\limits_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\Big|(f* (2^j\check{\varphi}(2^j\cdot)))\big(x-\frac{t}{2^j} \big)\Big|\,.
nodes.label: shif_maxM

nodes.name: $(n,\gamma_t)$-shifted square function and maximal function
nodes.statement: If $\frac{1}{4} <|t|<1$, $\varphi\in C^\infty_0$ with $\varphi(0)=0$, $n\in\mathbb{Z} $ and $\gamma\in\mathcal{NF}$ we define the $(n,\gamma_t)$-\emph{shifted square functions} with respect to $\varphi$ by \begin{equation} S_{n,\gamma_t}^{\varphi}f(x):=\Big(\sum\limits_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\Big|\Big(f*\big\{\frac{1}{\tfrac{2^{-j}\gamma'(2^{-j})}{2^n}} \check{\varphi} (\frac{\cdot}{\tfrac{2^{-j}\gamma'(2^{-j})}{2^n}})\big\}\Big) (x+\gamma(2^{-j}t))\Big|^2\Big)^\frac{1}{2}\,, \end{equation} and the $(n,\gamma_t)$-\emph{shifted maximal function} by \begin{equation} M^{(2^n)}_{\gamma_t}f(x):=\sup\limits_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\Big|\Big(f*\big\{\frac{1}{\tfrac{2^{-j}\gamma'(2^{-j})}{2^n}} \check{\varphi} (\frac{\cdot}{\tfrac{2^{-j}\gamma'(2^{-j})}{2^n}})\big\}\Big) (x+\gamma(2^{-j}t))\Big|\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Curve-adapted shifted square and maximal functions: the $j$-th piece is at scale $2^{-j}\gamma'(2^{-j})2^{-n}$ and shifted by $\gamma(2^{-j}t)$.

nodes.name: $(n,\gamma_t)$-shifted square function $S_{n,\gamma_t}^{\varphi}$
nodes.statement: S_{n,\gamma_t}^{\varphi}f(x):=\Big(\sum\limits_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\Big|\Big(f*\big\{\frac{1}{\tfrac{2^{-j}\gamma'(2^{-j})}{2^n}} \check{\varphi} (\frac{\cdot}{\tfrac{2^{-j}\gamma'(2^{-j})}{2^n}})\big\}\Big) (x+\gamma(2^{-j}t))\Big|^2\Big)^\frac{1}{2}\,,
nodes.label: shif_maxgama

nodes.name: $(n,\gamma_t)$-shifted maximal function $M^{(2^n)}_{\gamma_t}$
nodes.statement: M^{(2^n)}_{\gamma_t}f(x):=\sup\limits_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\Big|\Big(f*\big\{\frac{1}{\tfrac{2^{-j}\gamma'(2^{-j})}{2^n}} \check{\varphi} (\frac{\cdot}{\tfrac{2^{-j}\gamma'(2^{-j})}{2^n}})\big\}\Big) (x+\gamma(2^{-j}t))\Big|\,.
nodes.label: shif_maxgamaM

nodes.name: $p^*=\min\{p,p'\}$
nodes.statement: Throughout the paper $p^*=\min\{p,p'\}$ where $p'$ denotes de H\"older conjugate of $p$.

nodes.name: Positive part $a_+$
nodes.statement: Also we set $a_+:=\max\{a,0\}$.

nodes.name: $A\lesssim B$ notation
nodes.statement: For $A, B>0$, we say that $A\lesssim B$ if there is $C>0$ such that $A\le CB$.

nodes.name: $A\approx B$ notation
nodes.statement: We say that $A\approx B$ if $A\lesssim B$ and $B\lesssim A$.

nodes.name: $A\lesssim_d B$ notation
nodes.statement: Finally, if $d$ is a real parameter, we write $A\lesssim_d B$ if there exists $C=C(d)>0$ such that $A\le CB$ with the obvious correspondence for $A\approx_d B$.

nodes.name: Dyadic discretization of $M_\Gamma$
nodes.statement: Focusing now on the main subject, we record the following simple observation: since we deal with a positive integral operator, it is enough to study our maximal function with the supremum ranging over dyadic numbers, \textit{i.e.}, letting $\varepsilon\sim 2^{j+1}$ with $j\in\mathbb{Z}$, we have that \begin{equation} M_{\Gamma}(f,g)(x)\approx\sup\limits_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\frac{1}{2^{j+1}}\int\limits_{2^j\le|t|\le2^{j+1}} f(x-t)\,g(x+\gamma(t))\,dt. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3 Preliminaries: The bilinear maximal function as a multiplier operator; Reduction to the main component
nodes.statement_short: Since the operator is positive, the supremum can be restricted to dyadic $\varepsilon\sim2^{j+1}$.

nodes.name: Dyadic form of $M_\Gamma$
nodes.statement: M_{\Gamma}(f,g)(x)\approx\sup\limits_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\frac{1}{2^{j+1}}\int\limits_{2^j\le|t|\le2^{j+1}} f(x-t)\,g(x+\gamma(t))\,dt.
nodes.section: 3 Preliminaries: The bilinear maximal function as a multiplier operator; Reduction to the main component
nodes.label: discretization

nodes.name: Threshold $j_0$ for non-vanishing of $\gamma,\gamma',\gamma''$
nodes.statement: Based on the properties of the curves $\gamma\in\mathcal{NF}$ we have that\footnote{The condition discussed below will be needed when discussing the boundedness of our operator $M_{\Gamma}(f,g)$ in the regime $L^{\infty}\times L^q$ for $1<q\leq \infty$ - see Subsection 5.2.} \begin{align} \exists\:\:\textrm{(possibly large)}&\:\: j_0\in\mathbb{N}\:\:\textrm{depending only on}\:\gamma\:\textrm{such that} \\ \textrm{for any nonzero}&\:|t|\leq 2^{-j_0}\:\textrm{or}\:|t|\geq 2^{j_0}\:\textrm{one has}\nonumber\\ |\gamma(t)|>0,\:\: &|\gamma'(t)|>0,\:\:\textrm{and}\:\:|\gamma''(t)|>0\:. \end{align}
nodes.section: 3 Preliminaries: The bilinear maximal function as a multiplier operator; Reduction to the main component
nodes.statement_short: For $\gamma\in\mathcal{NF}$ there is $j_0$ with $\gamma,\gamma',\gamma''$ nonzero for $|t|\le2^{-j_0}$ or $|t|\ge2^{j_0}$.

nodes.name: Threshold property of $j_0$
nodes.statement: \exists\:\:\textrm{(possibly large)}&\:\: j_0\in\mathbb{N}\:\:\textrm{depending only on}\:\gamma\:\textrm{such that} \\ \textrm{for any nonzero}&\:|t|\leq 2^{-j_0}\:\textrm{or}\:|t|\geq 2^{j_0}\:\textrm{one has}\nonumber\\ |\gamma(t)|>0,\:\: &|\gamma'(t)|>0,\:\:\textrm{and}\:\:|\gamma''(t)|>0\:.
nodes.section: 3 Preliminaries: The bilinear maximal function as a multiplier operator; Reduction to the main component
nodes.label: threshold

nodes.name: Split of $M_\Gamma$ into $|j|>j_0$ and $|j|\le j_0$ parts
nodes.statement: M_{\Gamma}(f,g)(x)&\lesssim \sup\limits_{|j|>j_0}\frac{1}{2^{j+1}}\int\limits_{2^j\le|t|\le2^{j+1}} f(x-t)\,g(x+\gamma(t))\,dt\,\\ &+\,\sum_{|j|\leq j_0}\frac{1}{2^{j+1}}\int\limits_{2^j\le|t|\le2^{j+1}} f(x-t)\,g(x+\gamma(t))\,dt\,.
nodes.section: 3 Preliminaries: The bilinear maximal function as a multiplier operator; Reduction to the main component
nodes.label: discretizationsI

nodes.name: Bound for the finitely many scales $|j|\le j_0$
nodes.statement: Now for the latter term, using triangle and Minkowski's inequality, we trivially have \begin{align*} &\:\:\:\:\left\|\sum_{|j|\leq j_0} \frac{1}{2^{j+1}} \int\limits_{2^j\le|t|\le2^{j+1}} f(x-t)\,g(x+\gamma(t))\,dt\right\|_{L^r(dx)}\\ &\leq \sum_{|j|\leq j_0} \int\limits_{2^j\le|t|\le2^{j+1}} \|f(x-t)\,g(x+\gamma(t))\|_{L^r(dx)}\,\frac{dt}{2^{j+1}}\\ &\lesssim_{p,r} \,j_0\,\|f\|_p\,\|g\|_{q}\,, \end{align*} with $p,\,q,\,r$ satisfying \eqref{exponents10} and \eqref{exponents20}.
nodes.section: 3 Preliminaries: The bilinear maximal function as a multiplier operator; Reduction to the main component
nodes.statement_short: Triangle and Minkowski inequalities bound the $|j|\le j_0$ part by $j_0\|f\|_p\|g\|_q$.

nodes.name: Truncated bilinear maximal function ($|j|>j_0$)
nodes.statement: Thus, with a slight notational abuse, we will assume from now on that \begin{equation} M_{\Gamma}(f,g)(x)=\sup\limits_{{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\atop{|j|>j_0}}\frac{1}{2^{j+1}}\int\limits_{2^j\le|t|\le2^{j+1}} f(x-t)\,g(x+\gamma(t))\,dt. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3 Preliminaries: The bilinear maximal function as a multiplier operator; Reduction to the main component

nodes.name: Truncated dyadic $M_\Gamma$
nodes.statement: M_{\Gamma}(f,g)(x)=\sup\limits_{{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\atop{|j|>j_0}}\frac{1}{2^{j+1}}\int\limits_{2^j\le|t|\le2^{j+1}} f(x-t)\,g(x+\gamma(t))\,dt.
nodes.section: 3 Preliminaries: The bilinear maximal function as a multiplier operator; Reduction to the main component
nodes.label: discretizationc

nodes.name: Bump function $\underline{\rho}$
nodes.statement: Let now $\underline{\rho}$ be a nonnegative, even, $C^\infty_0(\mathbb{R})$ function with $\mathrm{supp} \underline{\rho} \subseteq\{t\in\mathbb{R}|\frac{1}{4}<|t|<1\}$ and \begin{equation} \int\underline{\rho}(t)dt=1\,. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3 Preliminaries: The bilinear maximal function as a multiplier operator; Reduction to the main component

nodes.name: Normalization $\int\underline{\rho}=1$ (Section 3)
nodes.statement: \int\underline{\rho}(t)dt=1\,.
nodes.section: 3 Preliminaries: The bilinear maximal function as a multiplier operator; Reduction to the main component
nodes.label: intones

nodes.name: Dilates $\underline{\rho}_j$
nodes.statement: Set $\underline{\rho}_j(t)=2^j\underline{\rho}(2^j t)$ (with $j\in\mathbb{Z}$).
nodes.section: 3 Preliminaries: The bilinear maximal function as a multiplier operator; Reduction to the main component

nodes.name: Smooth model $\mathcal{M}_\Gamma\approx M_\Gamma$
nodes.statement: With this, standard reasonings show that $M_{\Gamma}\approx \mathcal{M}_{\Gamma}$, where here \begin{equation} \mathcal{M}_{\Gamma}(f,g)(x):=\sup\limits_{{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\atop{|j|>j_0}}\mathcal{M}_{\Gamma,j}(f,g)(x):=\sup\limits_{{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\atop{|j|>j_0}}\int_\mathbb{R} f(x-t)g(x+\gamma(t))\underline{\rho}_j(t)dt\,. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3 Preliminaries: The bilinear maximal function as a multiplier operator; Reduction to the main component
nodes.statement_short: $M_\Gamma$ is comparable to the smoothed operator $\mathcal{M}_\Gamma=\sup_{|j|>j_0}\int f(x-t)g(x+\gamma(t))\underline\rho_j(t)dt$.

nodes.name: Smoothed operator $\mathcal{M}_\Gamma$
nodes.statement: \mathcal{M}_{\Gamma}(f,g)(x):=\sup\limits_{{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\atop{|j|>j_0}}\mathcal{M}_{\Gamma,j}(f,g)(x):=\sup\limits_{{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\atop{|j|>j_0}}\int_\mathbb{R} f(x-t)g(x+\gamma(t))\underline{\rho}_j(t)dt\,.
nodes.section: 3 Preliminaries: The bilinear maximal function as a multiplier operator; Reduction to the main component

nodes.name: Multiplier $m_j$ of $\mathcal{M}_\Gamma$
nodes.statement: Turning our attention on the Fourier side, we have that \begin{equation} \mathcal{M}_\Gamma(f,g)(x)=\sup\limits_{{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\atop{|j|>j_0}} \int_\mathbb{R}\int_\mathbb{R} \hat{f}(\xi)\hat{g}(\eta)m_j(\xi,\eta)e^{i\xi x}e^{i\eta x}d\xi d\eta\,, \end{equation} where the multiplier is given by \begin{equation} m_j(\xi,\eta):=\int_\mathbb{R} e^{-i\xi t}e^{i\eta \gamma(t)} \underline{\rho}_j(t)dt =\int_\mathbb{R} e^{-i\frac{\xi}{2^j} t}e^{i\eta \gamma(\frac{t}{2^j})} \underline{\rho}(t)dt. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3 Preliminaries: The bilinear maximal function as a multiplier operator; Reduction to the main component
nodes.statement_short: Writes $\mathcal{M}_\Gamma$ as a supremum of bilinear Fourier multipliers $m_j(\xi,\eta)=\int e^{-i\xi t}e^{i\eta\gamma(t)}\underline\rho_j(t)dt$.

nodes.name: Fourier representation of $\mathcal{M}_\Gamma$
nodes.statement: \mathcal{M}_\Gamma(f,g)(x)=\sup\limits_{{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\atop{|j|>j_0}} \int_\mathbb{R}\int_\mathbb{R} \hat{f}(\xi)\hat{g}(\eta)m_j(\xi,\eta)e^{i\xi x}e^{i\eta x}d\xi d\eta\,,
nodes.section: 3 Preliminaries: The bilinear maximal function as a multiplier operator; Reduction to the main component
nodes.label: M_multiplier

nodes.name: Multiplier $m_j(\xi,\eta)$
nodes.statement: m_j(\xi,\eta):=\int_\mathbb{R} e^{-i\xi t}e^{i\eta \gamma(t)} \underline{\rho}_j(t)dt =\int_\mathbb{R} e^{-i\frac{\xi}{2^j} t}e^{i\eta \gamma(\frac{t}{2^j})} \underline{\rho}(t)dt.
nodes.section: 3 Preliminaries: The bilinear maximal function as a multiplier operator; Reduction to the main component
nodes.label: M_multiplierr

nodes.name: Phase function $\varphi_{\xi,\eta}$
nodes.statement: Since the integrand in $m_{j}$ is highly oscillatory, the analysis of our multiplier relies fundamentally on understanding the stationary points of the phase function \begin{equation} \varphi_{\xi,\eta}(t):=-\frac{\xi}{2^{j}}t+\eta\gamma\big(\frac{t}{2^{j}}\big)\:. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3 Preliminaries: The bilinear maximal function as a multiplier operator; Reduction to the main component

nodes.name: Phase $\varphi_{\xi,\eta}(t)$
nodes.statement: \varphi_{\xi,\eta}(t):=-\frac{\xi}{2^{j}}t+\eta\gamma\big(\frac{t}{2^{j}}\big)\:.
nodes.section: 3 Preliminaries: The bilinear maximal function as a multiplier operator; Reduction to the main component
nodes.label: phmultiplier

nodes.name: Dyadic partition of unity $\phi$
nodes.statement: Let now $\phi$ be a positive even Schwartz function supported in $\{t:\frac{1}{2}\le|t|\le 2\}$ with $$\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\phi_n(t)=1\:\:\: \textrm{for all}\:\:\:t\not=0\,.$$
nodes.section: 3 Preliminaries: The bilinear maximal function as a multiplier operator; Reduction to the main component

nodes.name: Pieces $m_{j,m,n}$ of the multiplier
nodes.statement: Then, for every $j\in\mathbb{Z}\setminus [-j_0,\,j_0]$, we write \begin{equation} m_j=\sum_{m,n\in\mathbb{Z}} m_{j,m,n}, \end{equation} where \begin{equation} m_{j,m,n}(\xi,\eta):=m_j(\xi,\eta)\,\phi(\frac{\xi}{2^{m+j}})\,\phi\Big(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j})\eta}{2^{n+j}}\Big)\,. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3 Preliminaries: The bilinear maximal function as a multiplier operator; Reduction to the main component
nodes.statement_short: Localizes $m_j$ to $|\xi|\sim2^{m+j}$ and $|\gamma'(2^{-j})\eta|\sim2^{n+j}$.

nodes.name: $m_j=\sum_{m,n}m_{j,m,n}$
nodes.statement: m_j=\sum_{m,n\in\mathbb{Z}} m_{j,m,n},
nodes.section: 3 Preliminaries: The bilinear maximal function as a multiplier operator; Reduction to the main component

nodes.name: Definition of $m_{j,m,n}$
nodes.statement: m_{j,m,n}(\xi,\eta):=m_j(\xi,\eta)\,\phi(\frac{\xi}{2^{m+j}})\,\phi\Big(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j})\eta}{2^{n+j}}\Big)\,.
nodes.section: 3 Preliminaries: The bilinear maximal function as a multiplier operator; Reduction to the main component
nodes.label: mjmn

nodes.name: Low frequency, far-from-diagonal and close-to-diagonal components
nodes.statement: With this, we follow the approach in \cite{lie2015boundedness}, and split the analysis of our multiplier into three components, corresponding to the behavior of the phase in \eqref{phmultiplier}, as follows: \begin{enumerate} \item[I)] \underline{\emph{Low frequency case}} - the phase function is essentially constant: \begin{equation} m_j^L=\sum_{(m,n)\in(\mathbb{Z}_-)^2} m_{j,m,n}. \end{equation} \item[II)] \underline{\emph{High frequency far from diagonal}} - high oscillation without stationary points: \begin{equation} m_j^{H\not\Delta}=\sum_{(m,n)\in\mathbb{Z}^2\setminus((\mathbb{Z}_-)^2\cup\Delta)}m_{j,m,n}. \end{equation} \item[III)] \underline{\emph{High frequency close to diagonal}} - high oscillation with present stationary points: \begin{equation} m_j^{H\Delta}=\sum_{(m,n)\in\Delta}m_{j,m,n}. \end{equation} \end{enumerate} Here $\Delta=\{(m,n)\in\mathbb{Z}^2:m,n\ge0,|m-n|\le C(\gamma)\}$ with $C(\gamma)\ge 1$ a large constant depending only on $\gamma$.
nodes.section: 3 Preliminaries: The bilinear maximal function as a multiplier operator; Reduction to the main component
nodes.statement_short: Splits $m_j$ by $(m,n)$: both negative (low frequency), the diagonal band $\Delta=\{m,n\ge0,|m-n|\le C(\gamma)\}$, and the rest.

nodes.name: Low frequency multiplier $m_j^L$
nodes.statement: m_j^L=\sum_{(m,n)\in(\mathbb{Z}_-)^2} m_{j,m,n}.
nodes.section: 3 Preliminaries: The bilinear maximal function as a multiplier operator; Reduction to the main component
nodes.label: low_freq

nodes.name: High frequency far-from-diagonal multiplier $m_j^{H\not\Delta}$
nodes.statement: m_j^{H\not\Delta}=\sum_{(m,n)\in\mathbb{Z}^2\setminus((\mathbb{Z}_-)^2\cup\Delta)}m_{j,m,n}.
nodes.section: 3 Preliminaries: The bilinear maximal function as a multiplier operator; Reduction to the main component
nodes.label: high_far

nodes.name: High frequency close-to-diagonal multiplier $m_j^{H\Delta}$
nodes.statement: m_j^{H\Delta}=\sum_{(m,n)\in\Delta}m_{j,m,n}.
nodes.section: 3 Preliminaries: The bilinear maximal function as a multiplier operator; Reduction to the main component
nodes.label: high-close

nodes.name: Decomposition $m_j=m_j^L+m_j^{H\not\Delta}+m_j^{H\Delta}$
nodes.statement: m_j=m_j^L+m_j^{H\not\Delta}+m_j^{H\Delta}.
nodes.section: 3 Preliminaries: The bilinear maximal function as a multiplier operator; Reduction to the main component
nodes.label: multiplier

nodes.name: Linearizing function $j(x)$
nodes.statement: We end our preliminaries by transforming the maximal nature of our operator via a linearization procedure \begin{equation} \mathcal{M}_\Gamma(f,g)(x)\approx\int_\mathbb{R}\int_\mathbb{R} \hat{f}(\xi)\hat{g}(\eta)m_{j(x)}(\xi,\eta)e^{i\xi x}e^{i\eta x}d\xi d\eta \end{equation} where $j(x):\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{Z}\setminus [-j_0,\,j_0]$ is a measurable function who assigns for each point $x\in\mathbb{R}$ a value $j\in \mathbb{Z}\setminus [-j_0,\,j_0]$ for which $\mathcal{M}_{\Gamma,j}(f,g)(x)$ is at least half of the value of $\mathcal{M}_\Gamma(f,g)(x)$.
nodes.section: 3 Preliminaries: The bilinear maximal function as a multiplier operator; Reduction to the main component
nodes.statement_short: Linearizes the supremum: $j(x)$ is a measurable choice of scale at which $\mathcal{M}_{\Gamma,j}$ attains at least half of the supremum.

nodes.name: Linearized $\mathcal{M}_\Gamma$
nodes.statement: \mathcal{M}_\Gamma(f,g)(x)\approx\int_\mathbb{R}\int_\mathbb{R} \hat{f}(\xi)\hat{g}(\eta)m_{j(x)}(\xi,\eta)e^{i\xi x}e^{i\eta x}d\xi d\eta
nodes.section: 3 Preliminaries: The bilinear maximal function as a multiplier operator; Reduction to the main component
nodes.label: multiplier1

nodes.name: Theorem 3.1: low frequency term
nodes.statement: Set \begin{equation} \mathcal{M}^L_\Gamma(f,g)(x):=\int_\mathbb{R} \int_\mathbb{R} \hat{f}(\xi)\hat{g}(\eta)m_{j(x)}^L(\xi,\eta)e^{i\xi x}e^{i\eta x}d\xi d\eta. \end{equation} Then, the following holds \begin{equation} |\mathcal{M}_\Gamma^L(f,g)(x)|\lesssim_\gamma Mf(x)Mg(x). \end{equation} Furthermore, for any $p, q$ and $r$ satisfying \eqref{exponents10} and \eqref{exponents20} we have \begin{equation} \|\mathcal{M}_\Gamma^L(f,g)\|_r\lesssim_{\gamma,p,q}\|f\|_p\|g\|_{q}. \end{equation}
assumptions: for any $p, q$ and $r$ satisfying \eqref{exponents10} and \eqref{exponents20}
nodes.statement_short: The low-frequency component is pointwise dominated by $Mf\cdot Mg$, hence bounded $L^p\times L^q\to L^r$.
nodes.label: low_frequency_theorem

nodes.name: Low frequency operator $\mathcal{M}^L_\Gamma$
nodes.statement: \mathcal{M}^L_\Gamma(f,g)(x):=\int_\mathbb{R} \int_\mathbb{R} \hat{f}(\xi)\hat{g}(\eta)m_{j(x)}^L(\xi,\eta)e^{i\xi x}e^{i\eta x}d\xi d\eta.
nodes.label: operator_low_freq

nodes.name: Pointwise bound $|\mathcal{M}_\Gamma^L|\lesssim Mf\,Mg$
nodes.statement: |\mathcal{M}_\Gamma^L(f,g)(x)|\lesssim_\gamma Mf(x)Mg(x).
nodes.label: pointwise_maximal

nodes.name: $L^p\times L^q\to L^r$ bound for $\mathcal{M}_\Gamma^L$
nodes.statement: \|\mathcal{M}_\Gamma^L(f,g)\|_r\lesssim_{\gamma,p,q}\|f\|_p\|g\|_{q}.
nodes.label: pointwise_maximal_bound

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.1
nodes.statement:
Fix $m,n \in\mathbb{Z}_-$. From the definition of $\phi$ we have that $ ig| rac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}} ig|,  ig| rac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{j(x)}} ig|\lesssim 1$, and by property (3) as part of the definition of $\mathcal{NF}$ in \cite{lie2015boundedness}, we have \[ \sup\limits_{t\in\mathrm{supp}\underline{ho}}\Big|\eta\gamma\Big( rac{t}{2^{j(x)}} \Big)\Big|<C_\gamma, \] where $C_\gamma$ is a positive constant that is allowed to change from line to line. Recalling now \eqref{M_multiplierr} - \eqref{mjmn}, we develop the phase in \eqref{phmultiplier} in a Taylor series  egin{align} m_{j(x),m,n}(\xi,\eta)&=\Bigg(\int_\mathbb{R} \sum_{k\in\mathbb{N}}  rac{(-i rac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}t)^k}{k!}\sum_{l\in\mathbb{N}} rac{(i\eta\gamma( rac{t}{2^{j(x)}}))^l}{l\,!}\underline{ho}(t)dt\Bigg)\phi\Big( rac{\xi}{2^{m+j(x)}} \Big)\phi\Big( rac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{n+j(x)}}\Big)
onumber\ &=\sum_{k,l\ge0} rac{(-1)^k i^{k+l}}{k!\,l\,!}C_{k,l} \Big( rac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}\Big)^k\phi\Big( rac{\xi}{2^{m+j(x)}}\Big) \Big( rac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{j(x)}}\Big)^l\phi\Big( rac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{n+j(x)}}\Big), \end{align} where \[ C_{k,l}=C_{j(x),k,l}:=\int_\mathbb{R} t^k\Big( rac{\gamma(2^{-j(x)}t)}{2^{-j(x)}\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})}\Big)^l \underline{ho}(t)dt. \] Since  egin{equation} |C_{k,l}|\lesssim C_\gamma^{k+l} \end{equation} uniformly in $x$, the sum \eqref{taylor-series} converges absolutely. Set now  egin{equation} \psi(x):=\sum_{m<0}\phi( rac{x}{2^m})\,, \end{equation} and notice that $\psi\in\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R})$ since $\psi=1-\sum_{m\ge0}\phi_m.$ Inserting \eqref{taylor-series} in \eqref{low_freq} and recalling \eqref{notation21}, we have  egin{align} m^L_{j(x)}(\xi,\eta)&=\sum_{k,l\ge0}  rac{(-1)^k i^{k+l}}{k!\,l\,!}C_{k,l} \Big( rac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}\Big)^k\psi\Big( rac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}\Big) \Big( rac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{j(x)}}\Big)^l \psi\Big( rac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{j(x)}}\Big),\ &=\sum_{k,l\ge0}  rac{(-1)^k i^{k+l}}{k!\,l\,!}C_{k,l} \,	ilde\psi_k\Big( rac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}\Big) 	ilde\psi_l\Big( rac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{j(x)}}\Big). \end{align} Thus, putting together \eqref{lowTaylor} and \eqref{operator_low_freq} and recalling \eqref{notation22}, we have  egin{align} \mathcal{M}_\Gamma^L(f,g)(x)&=\sum_{k,l\ge0}  rac{(-1)^k i^{k+l}}{k!\,l\,!}C_{k,l} \Big(\int_\mathbb{R} \hat{f}(\xi)	ilde\psi_k\Big( rac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}\Big)e^{i\xi x}d\xi\Big) \Big(\int_\mathbb{R} \hat{g}(\eta)	ilde\psi_l\Big( rac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{j(x)}}\Big) e^{i\eta x}d\eta\Big)
onumber\ &\approx\sum_{k,l\ge0}  rac{(-1)^k }{k!\,l\,!}C_{k,l} \Big(f*\Big\{ rac{1}{2^{-j(x)}}\check{\psi}^{(k)}\Big( rac{\cdot}{2^{-j(x)}}\Big)\Big\}\Big)(x)\ &\hspace{2cm}	imes \Big(g*\Big\{ rac{1}{2^{-j(x)}\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})}\check{\psi}^{(l)} \Big( rac{\cdot}{2^{-j(x)}\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})}\Big)\Big\}\Big)(x).
onumber \end{align} We can construct the function $\phi$ such that for every $k\in\mathbb{N}$, the function $\check{\psi}^{(k)}$ has an integrable radially decreasing majorant $\Phi_k$ with $\|\Phi_k\|_1\lesssim C^k$ for some constant $C>0$. Thus, using a classical result in \cite{stein1993harmonic}, one has  egin{align} \Big|\Big(f*\Big\{ rac{1}{2^{-j(x)}}\check{\psi}^{(k)}\Big( rac{\cdot}{2^{-j(x)}}\Big)\Big\}\Big)(x)\Big|&\le \sup_{t>0} \Big|\Big(f*\Big\{ rac{1}{t}\check{\psi}^{(k)}\Big( rac{\cdot}{t}\Big)\Big\}\Big)(x)\Big|
onumber\ &\le \|\Phi_k\|_1 Mf(x)
onumber\ &\lesssim C^k Mf(x). \end{align} Analogously,  egin{equation} \Big|\Big(g*\Big\{ rac{1}{2^{-j(x)}\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})}\check{\psi}^{(l)} \Big( rac{\cdot}{2^{-j(x)}\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})}\Big)\Big\}\Big)(x)\Big|\lesssim C^l Mg(x). \end{equation} Putting together \eqref{low_frequency}, \eqref{Mf} and \eqref{Mg} we have  egin{align*} |\mathcal{M}_\Gamma^L(f,g)(x)|&\lesssim \sum\limits_{k,l\ge0} rac{1}{k!\,l\,!}|C_{k,l}|C^{k+l}Mf(x)Mg(x)\ &\lesssim Mf(x)Mg(x)\sum\limits_{k,l\ge0} rac{1}{k!\,l\,!}C_\gamma^{k+l} C^{k+l}\ &\lesssim_\gamma Mf(x)Mg(x),\addtocounter{equation}{1}	ag{	heequation} \end{align*} where here we used \eqref{constcont}. Therefore, \eqref{pointwise_maximal} holds. Taking now $p,\, q,\, r$ satisfying \eqref{exponents10} and \eqref{exponents20}, H"older’s inequality and the standard $L^p$ strong type estimate for the classical Hardy-Littlewood maximal function imply  egin{align*} \|\mathcal{M}_\Gamma^L(f,g)\|_r&\lesssim_\gamma\|Mf Mg\|_r\lesssim_{p,q} \|Mf\|_p\|Mg\|_q\lesssim_{p,q} \|f\|_p \|g\|_q, \end{align*} which concludes our proof.
nodes.statement_short: Taylor-expand the non-oscillating phase; each term factors into convolutions dominated by $C^kMf$ and $C^lMg$, summed by factorial decay, then Hoelder.

nodes.name: Taylor expansion of $m_{j(x),m,n}$
nodes.statement: m_{j(x),m,n}(\xi,\eta)&=\Bigg(\int_\mathbb{R} \sum_{k\in\mathbb{N}} \frac{(-i\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}t)^k}{k!}\sum_{l\in\mathbb{N}}\frac{(i\eta\gamma(\frac{t}{2^{j(x)}}))^l}{l\,!}\underline{\rho}(t)dt\Bigg)\phi\Big(\frac{\xi}{2^{m+j(x)}} \Big)\phi\Big(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{n+j(x)}}\Big)\nonumber\\ &=\sum_{k,l\ge0}\frac{(-1)^k i^{k+l}}{k!\,l\,!}C_{k,l} \Big(\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}\Big)^k\phi\Big(\frac{\xi}{2^{m+j(x)}}\Big) \Big(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{j(x)}}\Big)^l\phi\Big(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{n+j(x)}}\Big),
nodes.label: taylor-series

nodes.name: Bound $|C_{k,l}|\lesssim C_\gamma^{k+l}$
nodes.statement: |C_{k,l}|\lesssim C_\gamma^{k+l}
nodes.label: constcont

nodes.name: Definition of $\psi$
nodes.statement: \psi(x):=\sum_{m<0}\phi(\frac{x}{2^m})\,,
nodes.label: psi

nodes.name: Taylor form of $m^L_{j(x)}$
nodes.statement: m^L_{j(x)}(\xi,\eta)&=\sum_{k,l\ge0} \frac{(-1)^k i^{k+l}}{k!\,l\,!}C_{k,l} \Big(\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}\Big)^k\psi\Big(\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}\Big) \Big(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{j(x)}}\Big)^l \psi\Big(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{j(x)}}\Big),\\ &=\sum_{k,l\ge0} \frac{(-1)^k i^{k+l}}{k!\,l\,!}C_{k,l} \,\tilde\psi_k\Big(\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}\Big) \tilde\psi_l\Big(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{j(x)}}\Big).
nodes.label: lowTaylor

nodes.name: Series representation of $\mathcal{M}_\Gamma^L$
nodes.statement: \mathcal{M}_\Gamma^L(f,g)(x)&=\sum_{k,l\ge0} \frac{(-1)^k i^{k+l}}{k!\,l\,!}C_{k,l} \Big(\int_\mathbb{R} \hat{f}(\xi)\tilde\psi_k\Big(\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}\Big)e^{i\xi x}d\xi\Big) \Big(\int_\mathbb{R} \hat{g}(\eta)\tilde\psi_l\Big(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{j(x)}}\Big) e^{i\eta x}d\eta\Big)\nonumber\\ &\approx\sum_{k,l\ge0} \frac{(-1)^k }{k!\,l\,!}C_{k,l} \Big(f*\Big\{\frac{1}{2^{-j(x)}}\check{\psi}^{(k)}\Big(\frac{\cdot}{2^{-j(x)}}\Big)\Big\}\Big)(x)\\ &\hspace{2cm}\times \Big(g*\Big\{\frac{1}{2^{-j(x)}\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})}\check{\psi}^{(l)} \Big(\frac{\cdot}{2^{-j(x)}\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})}\Big)\Big\}\Big)(x).\nonumber
nodes.label: low_frequency

nodes.name: Maximal bound for the $f$ factor
nodes.statement: \Big|\Big(f*\Big\{\frac{1}{2^{-j(x)}}\check{\psi}^{(k)}\Big(\frac{\cdot}{2^{-j(x)}}\Big)\Big\}\Big)(x)\Big|&\le \sup_{t>0} \Big|\Big(f*\Big\{\frac{1}{t}\check{\psi}^{(k)}\Big(\frac{\cdot}{t}\Big)\Big\}\Big)(x)\Big|\nonumber\\ &\le \|\Phi_k\|_1 Mf(x)\nonumber\\ &\lesssim C^k Mf(x).
nodes.label: Mf

nodes.name: Maximal bound for the $g$ factor
nodes.statement: \Big|\Big(g*\Big\{\frac{1}{2^{-j(x)}\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})}\check{\psi}^{(l)} \Big(\frac{\cdot}{2^{-j(x)}\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})}\Big)\Big\}\Big)(x)\Big|\lesssim C^l Mg(x).
nodes.label: Mg

nodes.name: Pointwise bound summed over $k,l$
nodes.statement: |\mathcal{M}_\Gamma^L(f,g)(x)|&\lesssim \sum\limits_{k,l\ge0}\frac{1}{k!\,l\,!}|C_{k,l}|C^{k+l}Mf(x)Mg(x)\\ &\lesssim Mf(x)Mg(x)\sum\limits_{k,l\ge0}\frac{1}{k!\,l\,!}C_\gamma^{k+l} C^{k+l}\\ &\lesssim_\gamma Mf(x)Mg(x),\addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation}
nodes.label: pointwise_result

nodes.name: Bounded phase
nodes.statement: Fix $m,n \in\mathbb{Z}_-$. From the definition of $\phi$ we have that $\big|\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}\big|, \big|\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{j(x)}}\big|\lesssim 1$, and by property (3) as part of the definition of $\mathcal{NF}$ in \cite{lie2015boundedness}, we have \[ \sup\limits_{t\in\mathrm{supp}\underline{\rho}}\Big|\eta\gamma\Big(\frac{t}{2^{j(x)}} \Big)\Big|<C_\gamma, \] where $C_\gamma$ is a positive constant that is allowed to change from line to line.
nodes.statement_short: Fix $m,n<0$; the phase arguments are $O(1)$ on the support.

nodes.name: Taylor expansion
nodes.statement: Recalling now \eqref{M_multiplierr} - \eqref{mjmn}, we develop the phase in \eqref{phmultiplier} in a Taylor series \begin{align} m_{j(x),m,n}(\xi,\eta)&=\Bigg(\int_\mathbb{R} \sum_{k\in\mathbb{N}} \frac{(-i\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}t)^k}{k!}\sum_{l\in\mathbb{N}}\frac{(i\eta\gamma(\frac{t}{2^{j(x)}}))^l}{l\,!}\underline{\rho}(t)dt\Bigg)\phi\Big(\frac{\xi}{2^{m+j(x)}} \Big)\phi\Big(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{n+j(x)}}\Big)\nonumber\\ &=\sum_{k,l\ge0}\frac{(-1)^k i^{k+l}}{k!\,l\,!}C_{k,l} \Big(\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}\Big)^k\phi\Big(\frac{\xi}{2^{m+j(x)}}\Big) \Big(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{j(x)}}\Big)^l\phi\Big(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{n+j(x)}}\Big), \end{align} where \[ C_{k,l}=C_{j(x),k,l}:=\int_\mathbb{R} t^k\Big(\frac{\gamma(2^{-j(x)}t)}{2^{-j(x)}\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})}\Big)^l \underline{\rho}(t)dt. \] Since \begin{equation} |C_{k,l}|\lesssim C_\gamma^{k+l} \end{equation} uniformly in $x$, the sum \eqref{taylor-series} converges absolutely.
nodes.statement_short: Expand the phase in a double Taylor series with coefficients $C_{k,l}$ bounded by $C_\gamma^{k+l}$.

nodes.name: Define $\psi$
nodes.statement: Set now \begin{equation} \psi(x):=\sum_{m<0}\phi(\frac{x}{2^m})\,, \end{equation} and notice that $\psi\in\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R})$ since $\psi=1-\sum_{m\ge0}\phi_m.$
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the Schwartz function $\psi=\sum_{m<0}\phi(\cdot/2^m)$.

nodes.name: Sum over $m,n<0$
nodes.statement: Inserting \eqref{taylor-series} in \eqref{low_freq} and recalling \eqref{notation21}, we have \begin{align} m^L_{j(x)}(\xi,\eta)&=\sum_{k,l\ge0} \frac{(-1)^k i^{k+l}}{k!\,l\,!}C_{k,l} \Big(\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}\Big)^k\psi\Big(\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}\Big) \Big(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{j(x)}}\Big)^l \psi\Big(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{j(x)}}\Big),\\ &=\sum_{k,l\ge0} \frac{(-1)^k i^{k+l}}{k!\,l\,!}C_{k,l} \,\tilde\psi_k\Big(\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}\Big) \tilde\psi_l\Big(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{j(x)}}\Big). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Summing the expansion over $m,n<0$ writes $m^L_{j(x)}$ through $\tilde\psi_k,\tilde\psi_l$.

nodes.name: Factorized series for the operator
nodes.statement: Thus, putting together \eqref{lowTaylor} and \eqref{operator_low_freq} and recalling \eqref{notation22}, we have \begin{align} \mathcal{M}_\Gamma^L(f,g)(x)&=\sum_{k,l\ge0} \frac{(-1)^k i^{k+l}}{k!\,l\,!}C_{k,l} \Big(\int_\mathbb{R} \hat{f}(\xi)\tilde\psi_k\Big(\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}\Big)e^{i\xi x}d\xi\Big) \Big(\int_\mathbb{R} \hat{g}(\eta)\tilde\psi_l\Big(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{j(x)}}\Big) e^{i\eta x}d\eta\Big)\nonumber\\ &\approx\sum_{k,l\ge0} \frac{(-1)^k }{k!\,l\,!}C_{k,l} \Big(f*\Big\{\frac{1}{2^{-j(x)}}\check{\psi}^{(k)}\Big(\frac{\cdot}{2^{-j(x)}}\Big)\Big\}\Big)(x)\\ &\hspace{2cm}\times \Big(g*\Big\{\frac{1}{2^{-j(x)}\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})}\check{\psi}^{(l)} \Big(\frac{\cdot}{2^{-j(x)}\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})}\Big)\Big\}\Big)(x).\nonumber \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Express $\mathcal{M}_\Gamma^L$ as a series of products of convolutions with $\check\psi^{(k)}$, $\check\psi^{(l)}$.

nodes.name: Maximal function bounds
nodes.statement: We can construct the function $\phi$ such that for every $k\in\mathbb{N}$, the function $\check{\psi}^{(k)}$ has an integrable radially decreasing majorant $\Phi_k$ with $\|\Phi_k\|_1\lesssim C^k$ for some constant $C>0$. Thus, using a classical result in \cite{stein1993harmonic}, one has \begin{align} \Big|\Big(f*\Big\{\frac{1}{2^{-j(x)}}\check{\psi}^{(k)}\Big(\frac{\cdot}{2^{-j(x)}}\Big)\Big\}\Big)(x)\Big|&\le \sup_{t>0} \Big|\Big(f*\Big\{\frac{1}{t}\check{\psi}^{(k)}\Big(\frac{\cdot}{t}\Big)\Big\}\Big)(x)\Big|\nonumber\\ &\le \|\Phi_k\|_1 Mf(x)\nonumber\\ &\lesssim C^k Mf(x). \end{align} Analogously, \begin{equation} \Big|\Big(g*\Big\{\frac{1}{2^{-j(x)}\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})}\check{\psi}^{(l)} \Big(\frac{\cdot}{2^{-j(x)}\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})}\Big)\Big\}\Big)(x)\Big|\lesssim C^l Mg(x). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Radially decreasing majorants give each factor $\lesssim C^kMf$ and $\lesssim C^lMg$ (Stein).

nodes.name: Pointwise bound
nodes.statement: Putting together \eqref{low_frequency}, \eqref{Mf} and \eqref{Mg} we have \begin{align*} |\mathcal{M}_\Gamma^L(f,g)(x)|&\lesssim \sum\limits_{k,l\ge0}\frac{1}{k!\,l\,!}|C_{k,l}|C^{k+l}Mf(x)Mg(x)\\ &\lesssim Mf(x)Mg(x)\sum\limits_{k,l\ge0}\frac{1}{k!\,l\,!}C_\gamma^{k+l} C^{k+l}\\ &\lesssim_\gamma Mf(x)Mg(x),\addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation} \end{align*} where here we used \eqref{constcont}. Therefore, \eqref{pointwise_maximal} holds.
nodes.statement_short: Sum the factorially decaying series to get the pointwise bound.

nodes.name: Norm bound
nodes.statement: Taking now $p,\, q,\, r$ satisfying \eqref{exponents10} and \eqref{exponents20}, H\"older’s inequality and the standard $L^p$ strong type estimate for the classical Hardy-Littlewood maximal function imply \begin{align*} \|\mathcal{M}_\Gamma^L(f,g)\|_r&\lesssim_\gamma\|Mf Mg\|_r\lesssim_{p,q} \|Mf\|_p\|Mg\|_q\lesssim_{p,q} \|f\|_p \|g\|_q, \end{align*} which concludes our proof.
nodes.statement_short: Hoelder and the Hardy-Littlewood maximal theorem give the $L^r$ bound.

Set  egin{equation} \mathcal{M}^{H

ot\Delta}(f,g)\|_r\lesssim_{\gamma,p,q}\|f\|_p\|g\|_q. \end{equation} \end{itemize}

nodes.section: 3.2 High frequency term far from diagonal

nodes.name: Case 2: $n-m>C_\gamma$
nodes.statement: \textsf{Case 2}: $n-m>C_\gamma>>1$ $\newline$ As we did in Case 1, we write \[ \frac{1}{-\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}+\frac{\eta}{2^{j(x)}} \gamma'(\frac{t}{2^{j(x)}})} =\frac{1}{2^{n}}\frac{1}{\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{n+j(x)}}} \sum_{l\in\mathbb{N}}\frac{1}{2^{l(n-m)}} \Bigg(\frac{\frac{\xi}{2^{m+j(x)}}} {\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{n+j(x)}}}\Bigg)^l\frac{1}{(Q'(t)+Q'_{j(x)} (t))^{l+1}}. \] Write \[ \tilde{A}_{j(x),m,n}=\sum_{l\in\mathbb{N}}\tilde{A}_{j(x),m,n,l}, \] where \begin{align*} \tilde{A}_{j(x),m,n,l}(\xi,\eta)&=\frac{1}{2^{n}}\frac{1}{2^{l(n-m)}} \left(\int_\mathbb{R} e^{-i\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}t}e^{i\eta\gamma\big(\frac{t}{2^{j(x)}}\big)}i \frac{\underline{\rho}'(t)}{(Q'(t)+Q'_{j(x)}(t))^{l+1}}dt\right) \\ &\hspace{2cm}\times \tilde{\phi}_{l}\left(\frac{\xi}{2^{m+j(x)}}\right)\,\tilde{\phi}_{-l-1}\left(\frac{ \gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\,\eta}{2^{n+j(x)}}\right). \end{align*} Letting $\Lambda^{\tilde{A}}_{m,n,l}$ be the operator with symbol $\tilde{A}_{j(\cdot),m,n,l}$ one proceeds as before in order to get \begin{equation*} |\Lambda^{\tilde{A}}_{m,n,l}(f,g)(x)|\lesssim \frac{1}{2^n}\,\Big(\frac{C_{\gamma}}{2^{m-n}}\Big)^l\,\left(\int\limits_{\{\frac{1}{4} <|t|<1 \}} M^{(2^m t)}f(x)\,M^{(2^n)}_{\gamma_t} g(x)\,dt\right) \,, \end{equation*} and respectively \begin{equation} \|\Lambda^{\tilde{A}}_{m,n}(f,g)\|_r\lesssim_{\gamma,p,q} \frac{1}{2^n}(m_++10)\,(n_{+}+10)\, \|f\|_p\,\|g\|_{q}. \end{equation} Again, a similar reasoning applies to the multiplier $\tilde{B}_{j(\cdot),m,n}$.
nodes.statement_short: Case $n\gg m$: symmetric expansion gives decay $2^{-n}$.
nodes.section: 3.2 High frequency term far from diagonal

nodes.name: Geometric expansion (Case 2)
nodes.statement: As we did in Case 1, we write \[ \frac{1}{-\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}+\frac{\eta}{2^{j(x)}} \gamma'(\frac{t}{2^{j(x)}})} =\frac{1}{2^{n}}\frac{1}{\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{n+j(x)}}} \sum_{l\in\mathbb{N}}\frac{1}{2^{l(n-m)}} \Bigg(\frac{\frac{\xi}{2^{m+j(x)}}} {\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\eta}{2^{n+j(x)}}}\Bigg)^l\frac{1}{(Q'(t)+Q'_{j(x)} (t))^{l+1}}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Expand the reciprocal phase derivative in powers of $2^{-(n-m)}$.
nodes.section: 3.2 High frequency term far from diagonal

nodes.name: Pieces $\tilde A_{j(x),m,n,l}$
nodes.statement: Write \[ \tilde{A}_{j(x),m,n}=\sum_{l\in\mathbb{N}}\tilde{A}_{j(x),m,n,l}, \] where \begin{align*} \tilde{A}_{j(x),m,n,l}(\xi,\eta)&=\frac{1}{2^{n}}\frac{1}{2^{l(n-m)}} \left(\int_\mathbb{R} e^{-i\frac{\xi}{2^{j(x)}}t}e^{i\eta\gamma\big(\frac{t}{2^{j(x)}}\big)}i \frac{\underline{\rho}'(t)}{(Q'(t)+Q'_{j(x)}(t))^{l+1}}dt\right) \\ &\hspace{2cm}\times \tilde{\phi}_{l}\left(\frac{\xi}{2^{m+j(x)}}\right)\,\tilde{\phi}_{-l-1}\left(\frac{ \gamma'(2^{-j(x)})\,\eta}{2^{n+j(x)}}\right). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Decompose $\tilde A$ into pieces $\tilde A_{j(x),m,n,l}$.
nodes.section: 3.2 High frequency term far from diagonal

nodes.name: Bounds as in Case 1
nodes.statement: Letting $\Lambda^{\tilde{A}}_{m,n,l}$ be the operator with symbol $\tilde{A}_{j(\cdot),m,n,l}$ one proceeds as before in order to get \begin{equation*} |\Lambda^{\tilde{A}}_{m,n,l}(f,g)(x)|\lesssim \frac{1}{2^n}\,\Big(\frac{C_{\gamma}}{2^{m-n}}\Big)^l\,\left(\int\limits_{\{\frac{1}{4} <|t|<1 \}} M^{(2^m t)}f(x)\,M^{(2^n)}_{\gamma_t} g(x)\,dt\right) \,, \end{equation*} and respectively \begin{equation} \|\Lambda^{\tilde{A}}_{m,n}(f,g)\|_r\lesssim_{\gamma,p,q} \frac{1}{2^n}(m_++10)\,(n_{+}+10)\, \|f\|_p\,\|g\|_{q}. \end{equation} Again, a similar reasoning applies to the multiplier $\tilde{B}_{j(\cdot),m,n}$.
nodes.statement_short: Proceed as in Case 1 to get the pointwise and norm bounds with $2^{-n}$ decay.
nodes.section: 3.2 High frequency term far from diagonal

nodes.name: Sum over $(m,n)$
nodes.statement: Putting together all of the above, one concludes \begin{align*} \|M_\Gamma^{H\not\Delta}(f,g)\|_r &\lesssim_{\gamma,p,q} \sum_{\substack{(m,n)\in \mathbb{Z}^2\setminus((\mathbb{Z}_-)^2\cup\Delta)\\ m-n\geq C_{\gamma}}} \frac{1}{2^m}(m_++10)\,(n_{+}+10)\,\|f\|_p\,\|g\|_q\\ &\hspace{1cm} + \sum_{\substack{(m,n)\in \mathbb{Z}^2\setminus((\mathbb{Z}_-)^2\cup\Delta)\\ n-m\geq C_{\gamma}}} \frac{1}{2^n}(m_++10)\,(n_{+}+10)\,\|f\|_p\,\|g\|_q\\ &\lesssim_{\gamma,p,q} \|f\|_p\,\|g\|_q. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Sum the two cases over $(m,n)$ using the geometric decay.
nodes.section: 3.2 High frequency term far from diagonal

nodes.name: Theorem 3.5: high frequency term close to diagonal
nodes.statement: Set \begin{equation} \mathcal{M}^{H\Delta}(f,g)(x):=\int_\mathbb{R} \int_\mathbb{R} \hat{f}(\xi)\hat{g}(\eta)m_{j(x)}^{H\Delta}(\xi,\eta)e^{i\xi x}e^{i\eta x}d\xi d\eta. \end{equation} Then for any $p,\,q,\, r$ satisfying \eqref{exponents10} and \eqref{exponents20} we have \begin{equation} \|\mathcal{M}_\Gamma^{H\Delta}(f,g)\|_r\lesssim_{\gamma,p,q}\|f\|_p\|g\|_{q}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3.3 High frequency term close to diagonal
nodes.statement_short: The main (stationary-phase) component $\mathcal{M}^{H\Delta}$ is bounded $L^p\times L^q\to L^r$ in the full range.
nodes.label: high_frequency_diagonal theorem

nodes.name: Close-to-diagonal operator $\mathcal{M}^{H\Delta}$
nodes.statement: \mathcal{M}^{H\Delta}(f,g)(x):=\int_\mathbb{R} \int_\mathbb{R} \hat{f}(\xi)\hat{g}(\eta)m_{j(x)}^{H\Delta}(\xi,\eta)e^{i\xi x}e^{i\eta x}d\xi d\eta.
nodes.section: 3.3 High frequency term close to diagonal
nodes.label: operator_close

nodes.name: Norm bound for $\mathcal{M}_\Gamma^{H\Delta}$
nodes.statement: \|\mathcal{M}_\Gamma^{H\Delta}(f,g)\|_r\lesssim_{\gamma,p,q}\|f\|_p\|g\|_{q}.
nodes.section: 3.3 High frequency term close to diagonal
nodes.label: close_bound

nodes.name: Observation 3.6: identification with the bilinear Hilbert transform pieces
nodes.statement: Recalling Remark 2 in Section \ref{MIR}, since the mean zero condition in \eqref{mzh} plays no role in the regions where the phase of the multiplier is highly oscillatory, we are justified from now on to identify our operators $T_{j,m}$ and $B_{j,m}$ introduced below with the corresponding ones defined in \cite{lie2015boundedness}. Consequently, one can transfer with no modifications the theorems regarding $T_{j,m}$ and $B_{j,m}$ in \cite{lie2015boundedness} to our current setting.
nodes.section: 3.3 High frequency term close to diagonal
nodes.statement_short: Away from the low frequencies the mean zero condition is irrelevant, so $T_{j,m}$, $B_{j,m}$ and their theorems transfer from the bilinear Hilbert transform setting.
nodes.label: identif

nodes.name: Reduction of the main term to the operator $T$
nodes.statement: Using now the notation from \cite[Section 3]{lie2015triangle} and after some elaborate technicalities, one can prove that the study of the operator with multiplier $m_{j(x)}^{H\Delta}$ can be reduced to the study of the bilinear operator $T(f,g)$ defined by \begin{equation} T(f,g)(x):=\sum_{m\in\mathbb{N}}T_{j(x),m}(f,g)(x)\,. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3.3 High frequency term close to diagonal
nodes.statement_short: The operator with multiplier $m^{H\Delta}_{j(x)}$ reduces to $T(f,g)=\sum_m T_{j(x),m}(f,g)$.

nodes.name: Operator $T(f,g)$
nodes.statement: T(f,g)(x):=\sum_{m\in\mathbb{N}}T_{j(x),m}(f,g)(x)\,.
nodes.section: 3.3 High frequency term close to diagonal
nodes.label: T

nodes.name: Operators $T_{j,m}$ and multipliers $v_{j,m}$
nodes.statement: Here, for each $j\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $m\in\mathbb{N}$, we define \begin{equation} T_{j,m}(f,g)(x):=\int_\mathbb{R}\int_\mathbb{R}\hat{f}(\xi)\hat{g}(\eta)v_{j,m}(\xi,\eta)e^{i\xi x}e^{i\eta x} d\xi d\eta \end{equation} and \begin{equation} v_{j,m}(\xi,\eta):=2^{-\frac{m}{2}}e^{i\,\varphi_{\xi,\eta}(t_c)} \zeta\Bigg(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j})\eta}{2^{m+j}}, \frac{\frac{\xi}{2^{m+j}}}{\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j})\eta}{2^{m+j}}}\Bigg) \phi\Big(\frac{\xi}{2^{m+j}}\Big) \phi\Big(\frac{\gamma(2^{-j})\eta}{2^{m+j}}\Big) \end{equation} where we have \begin{itemize} \item the phase of the multiplier - recall \eqref{phmultiplier} - is defined as \begin{equation} \varphi_{\xi,\eta}(t):=-\frac{\xi}{2^j}t+\eta\gamma\big(\frac{t}{2^j}\big). \end{equation} \item For $\xi,\eta$ fixed, $\varphi_{\xi,\eta}$ has a unique critical point $t_c=t_c(j,\xi,\eta) \in [2^{-k(\gamma)},2^{k(\gamma)}]$, where $k(\gamma)\in\mathbb{N}$ depends only on $\gamma$. \item $\zeta:[\frac{1}{10},10]\times[2^{-k(\gamma)},2^{k(\gamma)}]\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfies $\|\zeta\|_{N-3}\lesssim 1$ for some $N\ge7$.\footnote{The regularity index $N$ here can be lowered but we will not detail this fact here.} \end{itemize}
nodes.section: 3.3 High frequency term close to diagonal
nodes.statement_short: $T_{j,m}$ is the bilinear multiplier with symbol $2^{-m/2}e^{i\varphi_{\xi,\eta}(t_c)}\zeta(\cdot)$ localized at frequency $2^{m+j}$, $t_c$ the unique critical point.

nodes.name: Operator $T_{j,m}$
nodes.statement: T_{j,m}(f,g)(x):=\int_\mathbb{R}\int_\mathbb{R}\hat{f}(\xi)\hat{g}(\eta)v_{j,m}(\xi,\eta)e^{i\xi x}e^{i\eta x} d\xi d\eta
nodes.section: 3.3 High frequency term close to diagonal
nodes.label: Tjm

nodes.name: Multiplier $v_{j,m}$
nodes.statement: v_{j,m}(\xi,\eta):=2^{-\frac{m}{2}}e^{i\,\varphi_{\xi,\eta}(t_c)} \zeta\Bigg(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j})\eta}{2^{m+j}}, \frac{\frac{\xi}{2^{m+j}}}{\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j})\eta}{2^{m+j}}}\Bigg) \phi\Big(\frac{\xi}{2^{m+j}}\Big) \phi\Big(\frac{\gamma(2^{-j})\eta}{2^{m+j}}\Big)
nodes.section: 3.3 High frequency term close to diagonal
nodes.label: vjm

nodes.name: Limits of $\gamma'$ at $0$ and $\infty$
nodes.statement: Also, from the properties of the class $\mathcal{NF}$, wlog we can assume that \begin{equation} \lim\limits_{\substack{t\to0\\ t\not=0}}\gamma'(t)=0\quad \text{ and } \quad \lim\limits_{t\to\infty}\gamma'(t)=\infty. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3.3 High frequency term close to diagonal

nodes.name: $\gamma'(t)\to0$ as $t\to0$, $\gamma'(t)\to\infty$ as $t\to\infty$
nodes.statement: \lim\limits_{\substack{t\to0\\ t\not=0}}\gamma'(t)=0\quad \text{ and } \quad \lim\limits_{t\to\infty}\gamma'(t)=\infty.
nodes.section: 3.3 High frequency term close to diagonal
nodes.label: lim

nodes.name: Rescaled operators $B_{j,m}$
nodes.statement: Thus, letting $\Psi_\eta(\xi)=-\varphi_{\xi,\eta}(t_c)$, we have \begin{itemize} \item For $j>0$ one sets \begin{equation} B_{j,m}(f(\cdot),g(\cdot))(x):=[\gamma'(2^{-j})]^\frac{1}{2}T_{j,m} \Big(f(2^{m+j}\cdot),g\Big(\frac{2^{m+j}}{\gamma'(2^{-j})} \cdot\Big)\Big)\Big(\frac{x\gamma'(2^{-j})}{2^{m+j}}\Big), \end{equation} that is \[ B_{j,m}(f,g)(x)=2^{-\frac{m}{2}}[\gamma'(2^{-j})]^\frac{1}{2} \int_\mathbb{R} \int_\mathbb{R} \hat{f}(\xi)\hat{g}(\eta)e^{i(\gamma'(2^{-j})\xi+\eta)x}e^{-i 2^m 2^{j}\Psi_{\frac{\eta}{\gamma'(2^{-j})}}(\xi)}\zeta(\eta,\frac{\xi}{\eta})\phi(\xi)\phi(\eta)d\xi d\eta. \] \item For $j\le 0$ one sets \begin{equation} B_{j,m}(f(\cdot),g(\cdot))(x):=[\gamma'(2^{-j})]^{-\frac{1}{2}}T_{j,m} \Big(f(2^{m+j}\cdot),g\Big(\frac{2^{m+j}}{\gamma'(2^{-j})} \cdot\Big)\Big)\Big(\frac{x}{2^{m+j}}\Big), \end{equation} that is \[ B_{j,m}(f,g)(x)=2^{-\frac{m}{2}}[\gamma'(2^{-j})]^{-\frac{1}{2}} \int_\mathbb{R} \int_\mathbb{R} \hat{f}(\xi)\hat{g}(\eta)e^{i(\xi+\frac{\eta}{\gamma'(2^{-j})})x} e^{-i 2^m 2^{j}\Psi_{\frac{\eta}{\gamma'(2^{-j})}}(\xi)} \zeta(\eta,\frac{\xi}{\eta})\phi(\xi)\phi(\eta)d\xi d\eta. \] \end{itemize}
nodes.section: 3.3 High frequency term close to diagonal
nodes.statement_short: $B_{j,m}$ is the rescaling of $T_{j,m}$ to unit frequency scale, with phase $2^m2^j\Psi$.

nodes.name: $B_{j,m}$ from $T_{j,m}$ for $j>0$
nodes.statement: B_{j,m}(f(\cdot),g(\cdot))(x):=[\gamma'(2^{-j})]^\frac{1}{2}T_{j,m} \Big(f(2^{m+j}\cdot),g\Big(\frac{2^{m+j}}{\gamma'(2^{-j})} \cdot\Big)\Big)\Big(\frac{x\gamma'(2^{-j})}{2^{m+j}}\Big),
nodes.section: 3.3 High frequency term close to diagonal
nodes.label: BTtr1

nodes.name: $B_{j,m}$ from $T_{j,m}$ for $j\le0$
nodes.statement: B_{j,m}(f(\cdot),g(\cdot))(x):=[\gamma'(2^{-j})]^{-\frac{1}{2}}T_{j,m} \Big(f(2^{m+j}\cdot),g\Big(\frac{2^{m+j}}{\gamma'(2^{-j})} \cdot\Big)\Big)\Big(\frac{x}{2^{m+j}}\Big),
nodes.section: 3.3 High frequency term close to diagonal
nodes.label: BTtr2

nodes.name: Functions $R$ and $R_j$
nodes.statement: From the definition of $\gamma\in\mathcal{NF}$ we define for $x\in\mathbb{R}$ \[ R(u):=\int_1^u r(s)ds \quad\text\quad R_{j}(u)=\int_1^u r_{j}(s)ds, \] then \[ 2^{j}\Psi_{\frac{\eta}{\gamma'(2^{-j})}}(\xi)=\eta R(\frac{\xi}{\eta})+\eta R_{j}(\frac{\xi}{\eta}). \]
nodes.section: 3.3 High frequency term close to diagonal
nodes.statement_short: $R(u)=\int_1^u r$, $R_j(u)=\int_1^u r_j$, so that $2^j\Psi=\eta R(\xi/\eta)+\eta R_j(\xi/\eta)$.

nodes.name: Model form of $B_{j,m}$
nodes.statement: B_{j,m}(f,g)(x):=2^{-\frac{m}{2}}[\gamma'(2^{-j})]^\frac{1}{2} \int_\mathbb{R} \int_\mathbb{R} \hat{f}(\xi)\hat{g}(\eta)e^{i(\gamma'(2^{-j})\xi+\eta)x}e^{-i 2^m \eta R(\frac{\xi}{\eta})}\zeta(\eta,\frac{\xi}{\eta} )\phi(\xi)\phi(\eta)d\xi d\eta.
nodes.section: 3.3 High frequency term close to diagonal
nodes.label: bjxm

nodes.name: Observation 3.7: the cutoff $\zeta$ can be replaced by $1$
nodes.statement: As in \cite[Section 5]{lie2015boundedness}, one can show that the function $\zeta$ above can be replaced by the constant function $1$. This brings a series of simplifications especially when dealing later with the situation $p\not=2$. Instead of following the argument in \cite[Section 5]{lie2015boundedness}, we present here a much simpler approach: the secret lies in changing the perspective and focusing on the function \[ \varrho(\xi,\eta):=\zeta(\eta,\frac{\xi}{\eta})\,. \] Indeed, by doing this, one can perform a double Fourier series development on $\varrho$ and notice that the linear complex exponentials will preserve the curvature of the phase given by $2^m\eta R(\frac{\xi}{\eta})$; in contrast with this, in the original argument focusing on $\zeta(\eta,\frac{\xi}{\eta})$, after the double Fourier series argument one had to work extra in order to deal with expressions of the form $\{\frac{\xi}{\eta}n_2\}_{n_2\in\mathbb{Z}}$. Returning now to the above definition of $ \varrho$ we notice that $\varrho:[\frac{2^{-k(\gamma)}}{10},10\cdot 2^{k(\gamma)}] \times[\frac{1}{10},10] \to\mathbb{R}$ satisfies $\|\varrho\|_{C^{N-3}}\lesssim_\gamma 1$. This last property follows from the fact that both $\xi$ and $\eta$ are away from $0$. We can now assume without loss of generality that $\varrho$ is compactly supported on $[2\pi,4\pi]\times[2\pi,4\pi]$. Regarding now $\varrho$ as a $2\pi$-periodic function on $\mathbb{R}^2$, we represent it as a multiple Fourier series: \[ \varrho(\xi,\eta)=\sum_{n_1,n_2\in\mathbb{Z}}c_{n_1,n_2}e^{i n_1 \xi}e^{i n_2 \eta}. \] From the hypothesis that $\|\varrho\|_{C^{N-3}}\lesssim_\gamma 1$ with $N\geq 7$, we have \begin{equation} |c_{n_1,n_2}|\lesssim_\gamma \frac{1}{(1+|n_1|+|n_2|)^4}. \end{equation} Thus, for $j>0$, it follows that \begin{equation} B_{j,m}(f,g)(x)=\sum_{n_1,n_2\in\mathbb{Z}}c_{n_1,n_2}B_{j,m}^{n_1,n_2}(f,g)(x) \end{equation} with \begin{equation} B_{j,m}^{n_1,n_2}(f,g)(x):=2^{-\frac{m}{2}}[\gamma'(2^{-j})]^\frac{1}{2} \int_\mathbb{R} \int_\mathbb{R} \hat{f}(\xi)\hat{g}(\eta)e^{i(\gamma'(2^{-j})\xi+\eta)x}e^{-i 2^m \eta R(\frac{\xi}{\eta})}e^{i\xi n_1}e^{i\eta n_2}\phi(\xi)\phi(\eta)d\xi d\eta. \end{equation} At this point we make the following simple observation: $\|B_{j,m}^{0,0}\|_{L^2\times L^2 \to L^1}=\|B_{j,m}^{n_1,n_2}\|_{L^2\times L^2 \to L^1}$ for any $n_1,\,n_2\in \mathbb{Z}$ since the factors $e^{i\xi n_1}$ and $e^{i\eta n_2}$ can be absorbed into the functions $\hat f$ and $\hat g$ in \eqref{BFourier1} without changing their corresponding $L^2$-norms. Consequently, since \eqref{z-coefficients} implies the absolute convergence of the sum $$\sum_{n_1,n_2}|c_{n_1,n_2}|\,\|B_{j,m}^{n_1,n_2}\|_{L^2\times L^2 \to L^1}=\|B_{j,m}^{0,0}\|_{L^2\times L^2 \to L^1}\,\sum_{n_1,n_2}|c_{n_1,n_2}|\,,$$ one realizes that the boundedness of each of $T_{j,m}$ can be thought as equivalent with the corresponding boundedness of $B_{j,m}^{0,0}$. Therefore, for notational simplicity, we redenote $B_{j,m}$ as $B_{j,m}^{0,0}$ and set $T_{j,m}$ as the correspondent operator associated with the newly defined $B_{j,m}$.
nodes.section: 3.3 High frequency term close to diagonal
nodes.statement_short: Expanding $\varrho(\xi,\eta)=\zeta(\eta,\xi/\eta)$ in a double Fourier series with summable coefficients reduces $B_{j,m}$ to $B^{0,0}_{j,m}$.

nodes.name: Decay of Fourier coefficients $c_{n_1,n_2}$
nodes.section: 3.3 High frequency term close to diagonal
nodes.label: z-coefficients

nodes.name: Fourier series expansion of $B_{j,m}$
nodes.section: 3.3 High frequency term close to diagonal
nodes.label: B-Fourier

nodes.name: Operators $B_{j,m}^{n_1,n_2}$
nodes.statement: B_{j,m}^{n_1,n_2}(f,g)(x):=2^{-\frac{m}{2}}[\gamma'(2^{-j})]^\frac{1}{2} \int_\mathbb{R} \int_\mathbb{R} \hat{f}(\xi)\hat{g}(\eta)e^{i(\gamma'(2^{-j})\xi+\eta)x}e^{-i 2^m \eta R(\frac{\xi}{\eta})}e^{i\xi n_1}e^{i\eta n_2}\phi(\xi)\phi(\eta)d\xi d\eta.
nodes.section: 3.3 High frequency term close to diagonal
nodes.label: BFourier1

nodes.name: Simplified $B_{j,m}$ (with $\zeta=1$)
nodes.statement: B_{j,m}(f,g)(x)=2^{-\frac{m}{2}}[\gamma'(2^{-j})]^\frac{1}{2} \int_\mathbb{R} \int_\mathbb{R} \hat{f}(\xi)\hat{g}(\eta)e^{i(\gamma'(2^{-j})\xi+\eta)x} e^{-i 2^m\eta R(\frac{\xi}{\eta})}\phi(\xi)\phi(\eta)d\xi d\eta\,,
nodes.section: 3.3 High frequency term close to diagonal
nodes.label: nbjxm

nodes.name: $\|B_{j,m}\|=\|T_{j,m}\|$ on $L^2\times L^2\to L^1$
nodes.section: 3.3 High frequency term close to diagonal
nodes.label: bt

nodes.name: Boundedness of $T$ on $\mathrm{int}(\triangle ABC)\cup(AB)$
nodes.statement: This together with interpolation imply the boundedness of the our main component operator $T$ for all triples $(\frac{1}{p},\frac{1}{q},\frac{1}{r'})$ within the interior of $\triangle ABC$ together with the edge $(AB)$, \emph{i.e.}, for all $p,\, q,\, r$ satisfying $\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}=\frac{1}{r}$ with $1<p,\, q<\infty$, and $1\le r<\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Bounds on the edges $(AB)$ and $(CD)$ plus interpolation give boundedness of $T$ for $1<p,q<\infty$, $1\le r<\infty$.

nodes.name: Lie's single-scale decay estimate (Theorem 3 of Lie 2015)
nodes.statement: {\cite[Theorem 3]{lie2015boundedness}} There exists $\epsilon\in(0,1)$ such that, for any $j\in \mathbb{Z}$ and $m\in\mathbb{N}$, one has \begin{equation} \|T_{j,m}(f,g)\|_{L^1}\lesssim_{\gamma} 2^{-\epsilon m}\|f\|_2\,\|g\|_{2}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Each $T_{j,m}$ maps $L^2\times L^2\to L^1$ with norm $\lesssim2^{-\epsilon m}$.
nodes.label: smallk2

nodes.name: Theorem 4.2: variable-scale $L^2\times L^2\to L^1$ decay
nodes.statement: There exists $\epsilon\in(0,1)$ such that, for any $m\in\mathbb{N}$, one has \begin{equation} \|T_{j(x),m}(f,g)(x)\|_{L^1(dx)}\lesssim_{\gamma} 2^{-\epsilon m}\|f\|_2\,\|g\|_{2}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The linearized operator $T_{j(x),m}$ keeps the $2^{-\epsilon m}$ decay $L^2\times L^2\to L^1$.
nodes.label: smallk20

nodes.name: Theorem 4.3: tame $L^p\times L^{p'}\to L^1$ bounds
nodes.statement: For any $m\in\mathbb{N}$ and \footnote{Throughout this subsection $q=p'$.} $p,\,p'$ satisfying $\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{p'}=1$ with $1<p<\infty$, one has \begin{equation} \|T_{j(x),m}(f,g)(x)\|_{L^1(dx)}\lesssim_{\gamma,p} m\,\|f\|_p\,\|g\|_{p'}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $T_{j(x),m}$ maps $L^p\times L^{p'}\to L^1$ with at most linear growth in $m$.
nodes.label: lpsmgr

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.5 for $r=1$
nodes.statement: Notice now that for the case $r=1$, our Theorem \ref{high_frequency_diagonal theorem} follows from Theorems \ref{smallk20} and \ref{lpsmgr} above via interpolation and geometric summation in the $m-$parameter.
nodes.statement_short: Interpolate the $2^{-\epsilon m}$ decay of Theorem 4.2 with the tame bound of Theorem 4.3 and sum geometrically in $m$.

nodes.name: Operator $T_m=\sum_j|T_{j,m}|$
nodes.statement: Before starting our journey, for $m\in\mathbb{N}$, we introduce the following operator: \begin{equation} T_m(f,g)(x):=\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}|T_{j,m}(f,g)(x)|\:. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Operator $T_m$
nodes.statement: T_m(f,g)(x):=\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}|T_{j,m}(f,g)(x)|\:.
nodes.label: Tm

nodes.name: Proof of Theorems 4.2 and 4.3 from Theorem 4.4
nodes.statement: We observe that one trivially has \begin{equation} |T_{j(x),m}(f,g)(x)|\leq T_m(f,g)(x)\:. \end{equation} We thus deduce that both Theorems \ref{smallk20} and \ref{lpsmgr} will be now direct consequences of the following
nodes.statement_short: Dominate $|T_{j(x),m}|$ pointwise by $T_m=\sum_j|T_{j,m}|$ and apply Theorem 4.4.

nodes.name: Theorem 4.4: bounds for $T_m$
nodes.statement: With the notations in \eqref{T}, \eqref{Tjm} and \eqref{Tm}, the following hold: \begin{enumerate} \item There exists $\epsilon\in(0,1)$ such that \begin{equation} \|T_{m}(f,g)\|_{L^1}\lesssim_{\gamma} 2^{-\epsilon m}\|f\|_2\,\|g\|_{2}. \end{equation} \item For $p,\,p'$ satisfying $\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{p'}=1$ with $1<p<\infty$, one has \begin{equation} \|T_{m}(f,g)\|_{L^1}\lesssim_{\gamma,p} m\,\|f\|_p\,\|g\|_{p'}. \end{equation} \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: $T_m$ has $2^{-\epsilon m}$ decay $L^2\times L^2\to L^1$ and at most linear growth in $m$ $L^p\times L^{p'}\to L^1$.
nodes.label: summ

nodes.name: Theorem 4.4 (1): $L^2\times L^2\to L^1$ decay of $T_m$
nodes.statement: There exists $\epsilon\in(0,1)$ such that \begin{equation} \|T_{m}(f,g)\|_{L^1}\lesssim_{\gamma} 2^{-\epsilon m}\|f\|_2\,\|g\|_{2}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Theorem 4.4 (2): tame bound for $T_m$
nodes.statement: For $p,\,p'$ satisfying $\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{p'}=1$ with $1<p<\infty$, one has \begin{equation} \|T_{m}(f,g)\|_{L^1}\lesssim_{\gamma,p} m\,\|f\|_p\,\|g\|_{p'}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Proof of (4.10): $L^2$ decay for $T_m$
nodes.statement: Using the following standard notation $\phi_{m+j}(\xi):=\phi\Big(\frac{\xi}{2^{m+j}}\Big)$ and $\phi_{\gamma,m,j}(\eta):= \phi\Big(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j})\eta}{2^{m+j}}\Big)$ we rewrite \eqref{l2c} in Theorem \ref{smallk2} as \begin{equation} \|T_{j,m}(f,g)\|_{L^1}\lesssim_{\gamma} 2^{-\epsilon m}\,\|f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}\|_2\,\|g*\check{\phi}_{\gamma,m,j}\|_{2}. \end{equation} Using this together with \eqref{Tm} we deduce that $$\|T_{m}(f,g)\|_{L^1}\leq \sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\|T_{j,m}(f,g)\|_{L^1}\lesssim_{\gamma} 2^{-\epsilon m}\,\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\|f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}\|_2\,\|g*\check{\phi}_{\gamma,m,j}\|_{2}$$ which, via an application of Cauchy-Schwarz, further gives $$\lesssim 2^{-\epsilon m}\,\left(\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\|f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}\|_2^2\right)^\frac{1}{2}\, \left(\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\|g*\check{\phi}_{\gamma,m,j}\|_{2}^2\right)^\frac{1}{2} \lesssim 2^{-\epsilon m}\,\|f\|_2\,\|g\|_2\,,$$ where in the last inequality we used that the supports of the functions $\{\phi_{m+j}\}_{\{j\in\mathbb{Z}\}}$ and respectively $\{\phi_{\gamma,m,j}\}_{\{j\in\mathbb{Z}\}}$ are almost disjoint, with the latter being a direct consequence of the properties of the curve $\gamma$ (see the property ``smoothness, no critical points, variation near $0$ and $\infty$" in the definition of $\mathcal{NF}$ in \cite{lie2015boundedness}).

nodes.name: Case 1: $1<p\le2$
nodes.statement: \textbf{Case 1.} $1<p\leq 2$ $\newline$ With the notations\footnote{We will only recall here that $\phi_{j,p_0}(\eta):= \phi(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j})\,\eta}{2^j}-p_0) $ and $\psi_{m,p_0,j}(\xi):= 2^{-\frac{m}{2}}\,e^{- i p_0 R(\frac{\xi}{2^j\,p_0})}\,\phi(\frac{\xi}{2^{m+j}})$ where $j\in\mathbb{N}$ and $p_0\in [2^m,\, 2^{m+1})\cap \mathbb{N}$ with $m\in\mathbb{N}$.} in \cite{lie2015triangle}, following the first part of the argument provided for the proof of Proposition 4.2 in Section 4 of \cite{lie2015triangle}, we have $$|\Lambda_{m}^{+}(f,g,h)|\lesssim$$ $$\int_{\mathbb{R}}\left( \sum_{j\in\mathbb{N}}|(f*\check{\phi}_{m+j})(y)|^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\: \left( \sum_{j\in\mathbb{N}} \left|M\left(\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(g*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})\,((\epsilon_{j,m} h)*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})|\right)(y)\right|^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\,dy$$ $$\lesssim \left\| \left( \sum_{j\in\mathbb{N}}|f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}|^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\|_{p}\, \left\|\left( \sum_{j\in\mathbb{N}} \left|M\left(\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(g*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})\,((\epsilon_{j,m}\, h)*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})|\right)\right|^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\|_{p'}$$ $$\lesssim \|f\|_{p}\,\left\|\left( \sum_{j\in\mathbb{N}}\left(\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(g*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})\,((\epsilon_{j,m}\, h)*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})|\right)^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\|_{p'}\:,$$ where for the last relation we used standard Littlewood-Paley theory (for providing bounds on the square function for $f$) and Fefferman-Stein's inequality (\cite{fefferman1971some}) (for the term involving the functions $g$ and $h$).
