nodes.name: Square function bound
nodes.statement: With the notations\footnote{We will only recall here that $\phi_{j,p_0}(\eta):= \phi(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j})\,\eta}{2^j}-p_0) $ and $\psi_{m,p_0,j}(\xi):= 2^{-\frac{m}{2}}\,e^{- i p_0 R(\frac{\xi}{2^j\,p_0})}\,\phi(\frac{\xi}{2^{m+j}})$ where $j\in\mathbb{N}$ and $p_0\in [2^m,\, 2^{m+1})\cap \mathbb{N}$ with $m\in\mathbb{N}$.} in \cite{lie2015triangle}, following the first part of the argument provided for the proof of Proposition 4.2 in Section 4 of \cite{lie2015triangle}, we have $$|\Lambda_{m}^{+}(f,g,h)|\lesssim$$ $$\int_{\mathbb{R}}\left( \sum_{j\in\mathbb{N}}|(f*\check{\phi}_{m+j})(y)|^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\: \left( \sum_{j\in\mathbb{N}} \left|M\left(\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(g*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})\,((\epsilon_{j,m} h)*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})|\right)(y)\right|^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\,dy$$ $$\lesssim \left\| \left( \sum_{j\in\mathbb{N}}|f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}|^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\|_{p}\, \left\|\left( \sum_{j\in\mathbb{N}} \left|M\left(\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(g*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})\,((\epsilon_{j,m}\, h)*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})|\right)\right|^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\|_{p'}$$ $$\lesssim \|f\|_{p}\,\left\|\left( \sum_{j\in\mathbb{N}}\left(\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(g*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})\,((\epsilon_{j,m}\, h)*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})|\right)^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\|_{p'}\:,$$ where for the last relation we used standard Littlewood-Paley theory (for providing bounds on the square function for $f$) and Fefferman-Stein's inequality (\cite{fefferman1971some}) (for the term involving the functions $g$ and $h$).
nodes.statement_short: Following Lie 2018, bound $\Lambda_m^+$ by square functions; use Littlewood-Paley and Fefferman-Stein.

nodes.name: $\ell^2$ control of $h$ pieces
nodes.statement: Using now that \begin{equation} ((\epsilon_{j,m}\, h)*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})(x)=\int_{\mathbb{R}} (\epsilon_{j,m}\, h)(x-\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j})}{2^j}\,y)\,\check{\phi}(y)\,e^{i\,p_0\,y}\,dy\:, \end{equation} we deduce that \begin{equation} \sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|((\epsilon_{j,m}\, h)*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})|^2\lesssim_{\gamma} \|h\|_{\infty}^2\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The $p_0$-sum of $|(\epsilon h)*\check\phi_{j,p_0}|^2$ is $\lesssim\|h\|_\infty^2$.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement: Thus, applying Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, we get \begin{equation} \left(\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(g*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})\,((\epsilon_{j,m}\, h)*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})|\right)^2\lesssim_{\gamma} \|h\|_{\infty}^2\,\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(g*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})|^2\,, \end{equation} from which we deduce that \begin{equation} |\Lambda_{m}^{+}(f,g,h)|\lesssim_{\gamma} \|f\|_{p}\, \|h\|_{\infty}\,\left\|\left(\sum_{j\in\mathbb{N}}\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|g*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0}|^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\|_{p'}\:. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz reduces to a square function of $g$.

nodes.name: Rubio de Francia
nodes.statement: Finally, since $p'\geq2$, we are allowed to apply Rubio de Francia's inequality (\cite{rubio1985littlewood}): \begin{equation} \left\|\left( \sum_{j\in\mathbb{N}}\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|g*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0}|^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\|_{p'}\lesssim_{\gamma,p'} \|g\|_{p'}\:. \end{equation} Putting now together \eqref{CS}, \eqref{L}, \eqref{RF} we conclude that \eqref{l2cppg} holds.
nodes.statement_short: Rubio de Francia's inequality bounds the square function of $g$, concluding Case 1.

nodes.name: Case 2: $2<p<\infty$
nodes.statement: \textbf{Case 2.} $2<p<\infty$ $\newline$ In this second case, we follow part of the argument inside the proof of Proposition 4.3 in Section 4 of \cite{lie2015triangle}. Indeed, by applying Cauchy-Schwarz and then H\"older's inequality, we have \begin{equation} \end{equation} $$|\Lambda_{m}^{+}(f,g,h)|\leq$$ $$\sum_{j\in\mathbb{N}}\int_{\mathbb{R}} \,\left(\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}*\check{\psi}_{m,p_0,j})(x)|^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\times \left(\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(g*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})(x)\,((\epsilon_{j,m}\, h)*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})(x)|^{2}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\,dx$$ $$\leq\left\|\,\left(\sum_{j\in\mathbb{N}}\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}*\check{\psi}_{m,p_0,j})|^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\|_{p} \left\|\left(\sum_{j\in\mathbb{N}}\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(g*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})\,((\epsilon_{j,m}\, h)*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})|^{2}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\|_{p'}\:.$$ Now the content of Proposition 4.4 in \cite{lie2015triangle} is the statement that for $p\geq2$ one has \begin{equation} \left\|\,\left(\sum_{j\in\mathbb{N}}\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}*\check{\psi}_{m,p_0,j}|^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\|_{p}\lesssim_{\gamma,p} m^{\frac{2}{p'}-1}\, \|f\|_{p}\;, \end{equation} while from the Lemma 4.9 in \cite{lie2015triangle} we deduce that \begin{equation} \sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(g*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})(x)\,((\epsilon_{j,m}\, h)*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})(x)|^{2}\lesssim_{\gamma} \|h\|_{\infty}^2\, M(g*\check{\phi}_{\gamma,m,j})^2(x)\:, \end{equation} where here we recall that $\phi_{\gamma,m,j}(\eta):=\phi(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j})}{2^{j+m}}\,\eta)\;.$ Inserting \eqref{Cf} and \eqref{claim} in \eqref{key2}, we conclude that \begin{equation} \end{equation} $$|\Lambda_{m}^{+}(f,g,h)|\leq_{\gamma,p} m^{\frac{2}{p'}-1}\, \|f\|_{p}\,\|h\|_{\infty}\, \left\|\left(\sum_{j\in\mathbb{N}} M(g*\check{\phi}_{\gamma,m,j})^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\|_{p'}$$ $$\lesssim_{p} m^{\frac{2}{p'}-1}\, \|f\|_{p}\,\|h\|_{\infty}\, \left\|\left(\sum_{j\in\mathbb{N}} (g*\check{\phi}_{\gamma,m,j})^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\|_{p'}\lesssim_{\gamma,p} m^{\frac{2}{p'}-1}\, \|f\|_{p}\,\|g\|_{p'}\,\|h\|_{\infty}\,,$$ where we made use again of the Fefferman-Stein's inequality (\cite{fefferman1971some}) (for the second inequality) and standard Littlewood-Paley theory (for the third inequality).
nodes.statement_short: Case $2<p<\infty$: Cauchy-Schwarz and Hoelder, then Lie's square function bound and Fefferman-Stein.

nodes.name: Follow Proposition 4.3 of Lie 2018
nodes.statement: In this second case, we follow part of the argument inside the proof of Proposition 4.3 in Section 4 of \cite{lie2015triangle}.
nodes.statement_short: Follow the proof of Proposition 4.3 in Lie 2018.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz and Hoelder
nodes.statement: Indeed, by applying Cauchy-Schwarz and then H\"older's inequality, we have \begin{equation} \end{equation} $$|\Lambda_{m}^{+}(f,g,h)|\leq$$ $$\sum_{j\in\mathbb{N}}\int_{\mathbb{R}} \,\left(\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}*\check{\psi}_{m,p_0,j})(x)|^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\times \left(\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(g*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})(x)\,((\epsilon_{j,m}\, h)*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})(x)|^{2}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\,dx$$ $$\leq\left\|\,\left(\sum_{j\in\mathbb{N}}\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}*\check{\psi}_{m,p_0,j})|^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\|_{p} \left\|\left(\sum_{j\in\mathbb{N}}\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(g*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})\,((\epsilon_{j,m}\, h)*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})|^{2}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\|_{p'}\:.$$
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\Lambda_m^+$ by a product of two square function norms.

nodes.name: Proposition 4.4 and Lemma 4.9 of Lie 2018
nodes.statement: Now the content of Proposition 4.4 in \cite{lie2015triangle} is the statement that for $p\geq2$ one has \begin{equation} \left\|\,\left(\sum_{j\in\mathbb{N}}\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}*\check{\psi}_{m,p_0,j}|^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\|_{p}\lesssim_{\gamma,p} m^{\frac{2}{p'}-1}\, \|f\|_{p}\;, \end{equation} while from the Lemma 4.9 in \cite{lie2015triangle} we deduce that \begin{equation} \sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(g*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})(x)\,((\epsilon_{j,m}\, h)*\check{\phi}_{j,p_0})(x)|^{2}\lesssim_{\gamma} \|h\|_{\infty}^2\, M(g*\check{\phi}_{\gamma,m,j})^2(x)\:, \end{equation} where here we recall that $\phi_{\gamma,m,j}(\eta):=\phi(\frac{\gamma'(2^{-j})}{2^{j+m}}\,\eta)\;.$
nodes.statement_short: Bound the $f$ square function by $m^{2/p'-1}\|f\|_p$ and the $g,h$ part by $M(g*\check\phi_{\gamma,m,j})$.

nodes.name: Conclude Case 2
nodes.statement: Inserting \eqref{Cf} and \eqref{claim} in \eqref{key2}, we conclude that \begin{equation} \end{equation} $$|\Lambda_{m}^{+}(f,g,h)|\leq_{\gamma,p} m^{\frac{2}{p'}-1}\, \|f\|_{p}\,\|h\|_{\infty}\, \left\|\left(\sum_{j\in\mathbb{N}} M(g*\check{\phi}_{\gamma,m,j})^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\|_{p'}$$ $$\lesssim_{p} m^{\frac{2}{p'}-1}\, \|f\|_{p}\,\|h\|_{\infty}\, \left\|\left(\sum_{j\in\mathbb{N}} (g*\check{\phi}_{\gamma,m,j})^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\|_{p'}\lesssim_{\gamma,p} m^{\frac{2}{p'}-1}\, \|f\|_{p}\,\|g\|_{p'}\,\|h\|_{\infty}\,,$$ where we made use again of the Fefferman-Stein's inequality (\cite{fefferman1971some}) (for the second inequality) and standard Littlewood-Paley theory (for the third inequality).
nodes.statement_short: Fefferman-Stein and Littlewood-Paley finish the bound.

nodes.name: Theorem 4.5: bounds on the segment $(CD)$
nodes.statement: Let $1\le r<\infty$. For $m\in\mathbb{N}$, the following holds \begin{equation} \|T_{j(x),m}(f,g)(x)\|_{L^r(dx)}\lesssim_{\gamma,r}(1+m^{1-\frac{1}{r}})\,2^{-\frac{m}{20r}}\,\|f\|_{2r}\,\|g\|_{2r}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: On $p=q=2r$, $T_{j(x),m}$ maps $L^{2r}\times L^{2r}\to L^r$ with decay $2^{-m/(20r)}$ up to polynomial factors.
nodes.label: 2r

nodes.name: Proposition 4.6: single-scale $L^p\times L^q\to L^r$ decay of $T_{j,m}$
nodes.statement: Let $p, q, r$ be as in \eqref{exponents10} and \eqref{exponents20}. Then for any $j, m\in\mathbb{Z}$, we have \begin{equation} \|T_{j,m}(f,g)\|_r\lesssim_{\gamma,p,q}(1+m^{1-\frac{2}{p}})\,2^{-\frac{m}{10}(1-\frac{1}{p*})}\,\|f\|_p\,\|g\|_q. \end{equation}
assumptions: Let $p, q, r$ be as in \eqref{exponents10} and \eqref{exponents20}.
nodes.statement_short: Each $T_{j,m}$ is bounded $L^p\times L^q\to L^r$ with exponential decay in $m$.
nodes.label: Tjmb

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.6
nodes.statement: Using the notation from (\ref{Ljm}) and \cite{lie2015triangle}, we choose $h\in L^{r'}$ such that \[ \Lambda_{j,m}(f,g,h)= \int_\mathbb{R} T_{j,m}(f,g)(x)h(x)dx. \] Therefore \[ |\Lambda_{j,m}(f,g,h)|\le \int_\mathbb{R} |(f*\check{\phi}_{m+j})(x)\:|M\Bigg(\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(g*\check{\phi}_{j, p_0})(\cdot) (h*\check{\phi}_{j, p_0})(\cdot)|\Bigg)(x)\,dx, \] and \[ |\Lambda_{j,m}(f,g,h)|\le \int_\mathbb{R}\Bigg(\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(g*\check{\phi}_{j, p_0})(x)(h*\check{\phi}_{j, p_0})(x)|^2\Bigg)^\frac{1}{2} \Bigg(\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}*\check{\psi}_{m, p_0, j})(x)|^2\Bigg)^\frac{1}{2}dx. \] Hence, by following the second part of the proof of \cite[Proposition 4.2 ]{lie2015triangle} and \cite[Proposition 4.3 ]{lie2015triangle}, we deduce that the results in \cite{lie2015triangle} hold for $\Lambda_{j,m}$. In particular, the analogue of \cite[Theorem 3.3]{lie2015triangle} follows: \begin{proposition} Let $1<p<\infty$. Then the following estimates hold \begin{equation} Edge\:(AC):\:\:\:\:\:\:\:\:|\Lambda_{j,m}(f,g,h)|\lesssim_{\gamma,p} (1+m^{1-\frac{2}{p}})2^{-\frac{m}{10}(1-\frac{1}{p*})}\|f\|_p\|g\|_\infty \|h\|_{p'}, \end{equation} and \begin{equation} Edge\:(AB):\:\:\:\:\:\:\:\:|\Lambda_{j,m}(f,g,h)|\lesssim_{\gamma,p} (1+m^{1-\frac{2}{p}})2^{-\frac{m}{10}(1-\frac{1}{p*})} \|f\|_p\|g\|_{p'} \|h\|_\infty. \end{equation} \end{proposition} Thus, Proposition \ref{Tjmb} follows from the Proposition \ref{DeltaM} after applying real interpolation.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the form $\Lambda_{j,m}$ as in Lie 2018 to get edge estimates on $(AC)$ and $(AB)$ (Proposition 4.7), then real interpolation.

nodes.name: Proposition 4.7: edge estimates for $\Lambda_{j,m}$
nodes.statement: Let $1<p<\infty$. Then the following estimates hold \begin{equation} Edge\:(AC):\:\:\:\:\:\:\:\:|\Lambda_{j,m}(f,g,h)|\lesssim_{\gamma,p} (1+m^{1-\frac{2}{p}})2^{-\frac{m}{10}(1-\frac{1}{p*})}\|f\|_p\|g\|_\infty \|h\|_{p'}, \end{equation} and \begin{equation} Edge\:(AB):\:\:\:\:\:\:\:\:|\Lambda_{j,m}(f,g,h)|\lesssim_{\gamma,p} (1+m^{1-\frac{2}{p}})2^{-\frac{m}{10}(1-\frac{1}{p*})} \|f\|_p\|g\|_{p'} \|h\|_\infty. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Decay estimates for the form $\Lambda_{j,m}$ on the edges $(AC)$ and $(AB)$, analogue of Theorem 3.3 of Lie 2018.
nodes.label: DeltaM

nodes.name: Dual function $h$
nodes.statement: Using the notation from (\ref{Ljm}) and \cite{lie2015triangle}, we choose $h\in L^{r'}$ such that \[ \Lambda_{j,m}(f,g,h)= \int_\mathbb{R} T_{j,m}(f,g)(x)h(x)dx. \]
nodes.statement_short: Choose $h\in L^{r'}$ dualizing $T_{j,m}(f,g)$.

nodes.name: Two bounds for $\Lambda_{j,m}$
nodes.statement: Therefore \[ |\Lambda_{j,m}(f,g,h)|\le \int_\mathbb{R} |(f*\check{\phi}_{m+j})(x)\:|M\Bigg(\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(g*\check{\phi}_{j, p_0})(\cdot) (h*\check{\phi}_{j, p_0})(\cdot)|\Bigg)(x)\,dx, \] and \[ |\Lambda_{j,m}(f,g,h)|\le \int_\mathbb{R}\Bigg(\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(g*\check{\phi}_{j, p_0})(x)(h*\check{\phi}_{j, p_0})(x)|^2\Bigg)^\frac{1}{2} \Bigg(\sum_{p_0=2^m}^{2^{m+1}}|(f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}*\check{\psi}_{m, p_0, j})(x)|^2\Bigg)^\frac{1}{2}dx. \]
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\Lambda_{j,m}$ by a maximal-function expression and by a square-function expression.

nodes.name: Results of Lie 2018 apply
nodes.statement: Hence, by following the second part of the proof of \cite[Proposition 4.2 ]{lie2015triangle} and \cite[Proposition 4.3 ]{lie2015triangle}, we deduce that the results in \cite{lie2015triangle} hold for $\Lambda_{j,m}$.
nodes.statement_short: The arguments of Propositions 4.2-4.3 of Lie 2018 apply to $\Lambda_{j,m}$.

nodes.name: Proposition 4.7
nodes.statement: In particular, the analogue of \cite[Theorem 3.3]{lie2015triangle} follows: \begin{proposition} Let $1<p<\infty$. Then the following estimates hold \begin{equation} Edge\:(AC):\:\:\:\:\:\:\:\:|\Lambda_{j,m}(f,g,h)|\lesssim_{\gamma,p} (1+m^{1-\frac{2}{p}})2^{-\frac{m}{10}(1-\frac{1}{p*})}\|f\|_p\|g\|_\infty \|h\|_{p'}, \end{equation} and \begin{equation} Edge\:(AB):\:\:\:\:\:\:\:\:|\Lambda_{j,m}(f,g,h)|\lesssim_{\gamma,p} (1+m^{1-\frac{2}{p}})2^{-\frac{m}{10}(1-\frac{1}{p*})} \|f\|_p\|g\|_{p'} \|h\|_\infty. \end{equation} \end{proposition}
nodes.statement_short: State the edge estimates (Proposition 4.7).

nodes.name: Interpolation
nodes.statement: Thus, Proposition \ref{Tjmb} follows from the Proposition \ref{DeltaM} after applying real interpolation.
nodes.statement_short: Real interpolation between the edge estimates.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.5
nodes.statement_short: Write Proposition 4.6 with localized inputs for $p=q=2r$, bound $|T_{j(x),m}|$ by an $\ell^r$ sum over $j$, and close with Hoelder, Cauchy-Schwarz and Littlewood-Paley.

nodes.name: Localized $L^{2r}$ decay of $T_{j,m}$
nodes.statement: \|T_{j,m}(f,g)\|_r\lesssim_{\gamma}(1+m^{1-\frac{1}{r}})2^{-\frac{m}{20r}}\|f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}\|_{2r}\|g*\check{\phi}_{\gamma,m,j}\|_{2r},

nodes.name: $\ell^r$ bound for $T_{j(x),m}$
nodes.statement: \big\|T_{j(x),m}(f,g)(x)\big\|_{L^r(dx)}&\le \Big(\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\|T_{j,m}(f,g)\|_r^r\Big)^\frac{1}{r}\nonumber\\ &\le (1+m^{1-\frac{1}{r}})2^{-\frac{m}{20r}} \Big(\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\|f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}\|_{2r}^r\|g*\check{\phi}_{\gamma,m,j}\|_{2r}^r\Big)^\frac{1}{r}.
nodes.label: supTjm

nodes.name: Square function bound for the $j$-sum
nodes.statement: \Big(\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\|f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}\|_{2r}^r\|g*\check{\phi}_{\gamma,m,j}\|_{2r}^r\Big)^\frac{1}{r}&\le \Big(\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\|f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}\|_{2r}^{2r}\Big)^\frac{1}{2r}\Big(\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\|g*\check{\phi}_{\gamma,m,j}\|_{2r}^{2r}\Big)^\frac{1}{2r} \nonumber\\ &\le_{\gamma,r} \|f\|_{2r}\|g\|_{2r}.
nodes.label: fg2r

nodes.name: Localized single-scale bound
nodes.statement: As we did for the proof of \eqref{l2c2}, we write \eqref{Tjm-pqr} as \begin{equation} \|T_{j,m}(f,g)\|_r\lesssim_{\gamma}(1+m^{1-\frac{1}{r}})2^{-\frac{m}{20r}}\|f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}\|_{2r}\|g*\check{\phi}_{\gamma,m,j}\|_{2r}, \end{equation} where here we used that $p=q=2r$ and that $(2r)^*=\frac{2r}{2r-1}$ since $r\ge 1$.
nodes.statement_short: Specialize Proposition 4.6 to $p=q=2r$ with frequency-localized inputs.

nodes.name: $\ell^r$ domination
nodes.statement: Since \begin{equation*} |T_{j(x),m}(f,g)(x)|\le \Big(\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}|T_{j,m}(f,g)|^r\Big)^\frac{1}{r}, \end{equation*} it follows from H\"older inequality and Proposition \ref{Tjmb} that \begin{align} \big\|T_{j(x),m}(f,g)(x)\big\|_{L^r(dx)}&\le \Big(\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\|T_{j,m}(f,g)\|_r^r\Big)^\frac{1}{r}\nonumber\\ &\le (1+m^{1-\frac{1}{r}})2^{-\frac{m}{20r}} \Big(\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\|f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}\|_{2r}^r\|g*\check{\phi}_{\gamma,m,j}\|_{2r}^r\Big)^\frac{1}{r}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Dominate $|T_{j(x),m}|$ by the $\ell^r$ sum over $j$ and apply Hoelder.

nodes.name: Littlewood-Paley
nodes.statement: Notice that for $r\in [1,\infty)$ and for any $f, \phi\in\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R})$, we have \begin{align*} \Big(\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\|f*\phi_j\|_{2r}^{2r}\Big)^\frac{1}{2r}&\le \Bigg(\int_\mathbb{R} \sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}|(f*\phi_j)(x)|^{2r}dx\Bigg)^\frac{1}{2r}\\ &\le \Bigg(\int_\mathbb{R} \Bigg(\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}|(f*\phi_j)(x)|^2\Bigg)^rdx\Bigg)^\frac{1}{2r} = \Bigg(\int_\mathbb{R} \Bigg\{\bigg(\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}|(f*\phi_j)(x)|^2\bigg)^\frac{1}{2}\Bigg\}^{2r}dx\Bigg)^\frac{1}{2r}\\ &=\Bigg\|\bigg(\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}|f*\phi_j(x)|^2\bigg)^\frac{1}{2}\Bigg\|_{2r} \lesssim \|f\|_{2r}, \end{align*} here for the last relation we used standard Littlewood-Paley theory.
nodes.statement_short: $\ell^{2r}$ sums of localized norms are controlled by the square function, hence by $\|f\|_{2r}$.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz in $j$
nodes.statement: By Cauchy Schwartz, the hypothesis on $\gamma\in \mathcal{NF}$ and the result above, we obtain \begin{align} \Big(\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\|f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}\|_{2r}^r\|g*\check{\phi}_{\gamma,m,j}\|_{2r}^r\Big)^\frac{1}{r}&\le \Big(\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\|f*\check{\phi}_{m+j}\|_{2r}^{2r}\Big)^\frac{1}{2r}\Big(\sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\|g*\check{\phi}_{\gamma,m,j}\|_{2r}^{2r}\Big)^\frac{1}{2r} \nonumber\\ &\le_{\gamma,r} \|f\|_{2r}\|g\|_{2r}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz in $j$ and the previous bound give $\|f\|_{2r}\|g\|_{2r}$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Inserting \eqref{fg2r} in \eqref{supTjm} we get \begin{equation} \big\|T_{j(x),m}(f,g)(x)\big\|_{L^r(dx)}\le_{\gamma,r} (1+m^{1-\frac{1}{r}})2^{-\frac{m}{20r}}\|f\|_{2r}\|g\|_{2r}, \end{equation} as desired.
nodes.statement_short: Combine to get the claimed bound.

nodes.name: Observation 4.8: the $(CD)$ bound is not needed for the interior
nodes.statement: In order to prove our main Theorem \ref{high_frequency_diagonal theorem} in the interior of $\triangle ABC$ it is in fact not necessary to pursue the boundedness of our operator along the edge $(CD)$. Indeed, one could apply interpolation between the bounds corresponding to the edges $(AB)$ and $(AC)$ instead, with the latter discussed in the next section. However, we wanted to offer a less expected but more interesting alternative approach to the trivial bounds one gets along the segment $(AC)$. This is especially useful in situations in which one deals with similar type operators but for which one does not have a good control on the edges $(BC)$ and $(AC)$.
nodes.statement_short: Interpolating between the edges $(AB)$ and $(AC)$ would also give the interior; the $(CD)$ route is an alternative useful when edge control is missing.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.1
nodes.statement: From the definition \eqref{definition} of $M_\Gamma$ it is trivial to notice that for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$, \begin{align} |M_\Gamma(f,g)(x)|&\le \|g\|_\infty\, \sup_{\varepsilon>0}\frac{1}{2\varepsilon}\int_{-\varepsilon}^\varepsilon |f(x-t)|dt\nonumber\\ &\le \|g\|_\infty\, Mf(x). \end{align} Hence, applying the classical results on the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator we get
nodes.section: 5.1 Bounds on the edge $(AC]$: $1< p\le \infty$, $r=p$ and $q=\infty$
nodes.statement_short: Pointwise $M_\Gamma(f,g)\le\|g\|_\infty Mf$, then the Hardy-Littlewood maximal theorem.

nodes.name: Pointwise bound $M_\Gamma(f,g)\le\|g\|_\infty Mf$
nodes.statement: |M_\Gamma(f,g)(x)|&\le \|g\|_\infty\, \sup_{\varepsilon>0}\frac{1}{2\varepsilon}\int_{-\varepsilon}^\varepsilon |f(x-t)|dt\nonumber\\ &\le \|g\|_\infty\, Mf(x).
nodes.section: 5.1 Bounds on the edge $(AC]$: $1< p\le \infty$, $r=p$ and $q=\infty$
nodes.label: 1inf1

nodes.name: Theorem 5.1: bounds on the edge $(AC]$
nodes.statement: For any $1<p\le \infty$, one has \begin{equation} \|M_\Gamma(f,g)\|_{L^p}\lesssim_p \|f\|_p\,\|g\|_\infty. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5.1 Bounds on the edge $(AC]$: $1< p\le \infty$, $r=p$ and $q=\infty$
nodes.label: ginfty

nodes.name: $L^p\times L^\infty\to L^p$ bound for $M_\Gamma$
nodes.statement: \|M_\Gamma(f,g)\|_{L^p}\lesssim_p \|f\|_p\,\|g\|_\infty.
nodes.section: 5.1 Bounds on the edge $(AC]$: $1< p\le \infty$, $r=p$ and $q=\infty$

nodes.name: Theorem 5.2: bounds on the edge $(BC]$
nodes.statement: For any $1<q\le \infty$, one has \begin{equation} \|M_\Gamma(f,g)\|_{L^q}\lesssim_{\gamma,q} \|f\|_\infty\,\|g\|_q. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5.2 Bounds on the edge $(BC]$: $1< q\le \infty$, $r=q$ and $p=\infty$
nodes.label: finfty

nodes.name: $L^\infty\times L^q\to L^q$ bound for $M_\Gamma$
nodes.statement: \|M_\Gamma(f,g)\|_{L^q}\lesssim_{\gamma,q} \|f\|_\infty\,\|g\|_q.
nodes.section: 5.2 Bounds on the edge $(BC]$: $1< q\le \infty$, $r=q$ and $p=\infty$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.2
nodes.statement: From \eqref{discretizationc}, recalling that $\gamma\in\mathcal{NF}$ and our choice of $j_0$ in \eqref{threshold} - \eqref{threshold1}, we notice that for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$, \begin{align} |M_\Gamma(f,g)(x)|&\le \|f\|_\infty\,M_\gamma\, g(x). \end{align} where here \begin{equation} M_\gamma\, g(x):=\sup\limits_{{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\atop{|j|>j_0}}\frac{1}{2^{j+1}}\int\limits_{2^j\le|t|\le2^{j+1}} |g(x+\gamma(t))|dt\,. \end{equation} Thus, Theorem \ref{finfty} follows from the result below
nodes.section: 5.2 Bounds on the edge $(BC]$: $1< q\le \infty$, $r=q$ and $p=\infty$
nodes.statement_short: Pointwise $M_\Gamma(f,g)\le\|f\|_\infty M_\gamma g$, reducing to the maximal function along $\gamma$ (Theorem 5.3).

nodes.name: Pointwise bound $M_\Gamma(f,g)\le\|f\|_\infty M_\gamma g$
nodes.statement: |M_\Gamma(f,g)(x)|&\le \|f\|_\infty\,M_\gamma\, g(x).
nodes.section: 5.2 Bounds on the edge $(BC]$: $1< q\le \infty$, $r=q$ and $p=\infty$
nodes.label: ginf

nodes.name: Maximal function along $\gamma$: $M_\gamma$
nodes.statement: M_\gamma\, g(x):=\sup\limits_{{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\atop{|j|>j_0}}\frac{1}{2^{j+1}}\int\limits_{2^j\le|t|\le2^{j+1}} |g(x+\gamma(t))|dt\,.
nodes.section: 5.2 Bounds on the edge $(BC]$: $1< q\le \infty$, $r=q$ and $p=\infty$

nodes.name: Theorem 5.3: maximal function along $\gamma$
nodes.statement: For any $1<q\le \infty$, one has \begin{equation} \|M_\gamma(g)\|_{L^q}\lesssim_{\gamma,q} \|g\|_q. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 5.2 Bounds on the edge $(BC]$: $1< q\le \infty$, $r=q$ and $p=\infty$
nodes.statement_short: The maximal function $M_\gamma$ along the curve is bounded on $L^q$, $1<q\le\infty$.
nodes.label: Mgamma

nodes.name: $L^q$ bound for $M_\gamma$
nodes.statement: \|M_\gamma(g)\|_{L^q}\lesssim_{\gamma,q} \|g\|_q.
nodes.section: 5.2 Bounds on the edge $(BC]$: $1< q\le \infty$, $r=q$ and $p=\infty$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.3
nodes.statement: From the properties of $\gamma$ and the choice of $j_0$ in \eqref{threshold} - \eqref{threshold1}, it is straightforward to check that for any $k\in \mathbb{Z}$ with $|k|>j_0$ and $t\in[2^k,2^{k+1}]$ one has \begin{equation} |\gamma(2^{k})|\approx_{\gamma} 2^{k}|\gamma'(t)|\approx_{\gamma}|\gamma(2^{k+1})|\,. \end{equation} From \eqref{threshold1}, we deduce that $\gamma$ is strictly monotone and invertible over each of the intervals $(-\infty,-2^{j_0})$, $(-2^{-j_0},0)$, $(0,2^{-j_0})$ and $(2^{j_0}, \infty)$. Wlog we consider from now on that our entire discussion takes place relative to $J_0:=(2^{j_0}, \infty)$ and that both $\gamma'$ and $\gamma''$ are strictly positive on $J_0$. Thus, for $k\in\mathbb{Z}$ with $k>j_0$, one has \begin{align*} \frac{1}{2^{k+1}}\int_{2^k}^{2^{k+1}}|g(x+\gamma(t))|dt &=\frac{1}{2^{k+1}}\int_{\gamma([2^k,2^{k+1}])}|g(x+u)|\frac{du}{|\gamma'(\gamma^{-1}(u))|}\\ &\le\frac{1}{2^{k+1}|\gamma'(2^k)|}\int_{\gamma(2^k)}^{\gamma(2^{k+1})}|g(x+u)|du\,. \end{align*} Appealing now to \eqref{gammak1t}, we deduce \begin{equation} \frac{1}{2^{k+1}}\int_{2^k}^{2^{k+1}}|g(x+\gamma(t))|dt \leq\frac{1}{2^{k+1}|\gamma'(2^k)|}\int_{-|\gamma(2^k)|-|\gamma(2^{k+1})|}^{|\gamma(2^k)|+|\gamma(2^{k+1})|}|g(x-u)|du \lesssim_{\gamma} Mg(x). \end{equation} Analogously, \begin{align*} \frac{1}{2^{k+1}}\int_{-2^{k+1}}^{-2^k}|g(x+\gamma(t))|dt&\lesssim_{\gamma} Mg(x). \end{align*} Therefore \begin{equation} \sup_{{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\atop{|j|>j_0}}\,\frac{1}{2^{j+1}}\int\limits_{2^j\le|t|\le2^{j+1}} |g(x+\gamma(t))|dt\lesssim_{\gamma} Mg(x). \end{equation} Using now the standard theory on Hardy Littlewood maximal operator we conclude our Theorem \ref{Mgamma}.
nodes.section: 5.2 Bounds on the edge $(BC]$: $1< q\le \infty$, $r=q$ and $p=\infty$
nodes.statement_short: Change variables $u=\gamma(t)$ on each dyadic interval; doubling of $\gamma$ beyond $2^{j_0}$ dominates each average by $Mg$.

nodes.name: Doubling comparison $|\gamma(2^k)|\approx2^k|\gamma'(t)|$
nodes.statement: |\gamma(2^{k})|\approx_{\gamma} 2^{k}|\gamma'(t)|\approx_{\gamma}|\gamma(2^{k+1})|\,.
nodes.section: 5.2 Bounds on the edge $(BC]$: $1< q\le \infty$, $r=q$ and $p=\infty$
nodes.label: gammak1t

nodes.name: Dyadic average bounded by $Mg$
nodes.statement: \frac{1}{2^{k+1}}\int_{2^k}^{2^{k+1}}|g(x+\gamma(t))|dt \leq\frac{1}{2^{k+1}|\gamma'(2^k)|}\int_{-|\gamma(2^k)|-|\gamma(2^{k+1})|}^{|\gamma(2^k)|+|\gamma(2^{k+1})|}|g(x-u)|du \lesssim_{\gamma} Mg(x).
nodes.section: 5.2 Bounds on the edge $(BC]$: $1< q\le \infty$, $r=q$ and $p=\infty$
nodes.label: ks

nodes.name: $M_\gamma g\lesssim Mg$
nodes.statement: \sup_{{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\atop{|j|>j_0}}\,\frac{1}{2^{j+1}}\int\limits_{2^j\le|t|\le2^{j+1}} |g(x+\gamma(t))|dt\lesssim_{\gamma} Mg(x).
nodes.section: 5.2 Bounds on the edge $(BC]$: $1< q\le \infty$, $r=q$ and $p=\infty$

nodes.name: Doubling of $\gamma$
nodes.statement: From the properties of $\gamma$ and the choice of $j_0$ in \eqref{threshold} - \eqref{threshold1}, it is straightforward to check that for any $k\in \mathbb{Z}$ with $|k|>j_0$ and $t\in[2^k,2^{k+1}]$ one has \begin{equation} |\gamma(2^{k})|\approx_{\gamma} 2^{k}|\gamma'(t)|\approx_{\gamma}|\gamma(2^{k+1})|\,. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: For $|k|>j_0$, $|\gamma(2^k)|\approx2^k|\gamma'(t)|\approx|\gamma(2^{k+1})|$.
nodes.section: 5.2 Bounds on the edge $(BC]$: $1< q\le \infty$, $r=q$ and $p=\infty$

nodes.name: Change of variables
nodes.statement: From \eqref{threshold1}, we deduce that $\gamma$ is strictly monotone and invertible over each of the intervals $(-\infty,-2^{j_0})$, $(-2^{-j_0},0)$, $(0,2^{-j_0})$ and $(2^{j_0}, \infty)$. Wlog we consider from now on that our entire discussion takes place relative to $J_0:=(2^{j_0}, \infty)$ and that both $\gamma'$ and $\gamma''$ are strictly positive on $J_0$. Thus, for $k\in\mathbb{Z}$ with $k>j_0$, one has \begin{align*} \frac{1}{2^{k+1}}\int_{2^k}^{2^{k+1}}|g(x+\gamma(t))|dt &=\frac{1}{2^{k+1}}\int_{\gamma([2^k,2^{k+1}])}|g(x+u)|\frac{du}{|\gamma'(\gamma^{-1}(u))|}\\ &\le\frac{1}{2^{k+1}|\gamma'(2^k)|}\int_{\gamma(2^k)}^{\gamma(2^{k+1})}|g(x+u)|du\,. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: On $J_0$, $\gamma$ is monotone; change variables $u=\gamma(t)$.
nodes.section: 5.2 Bounds on the edge $(BC]$: $1< q\le \infty$, $r=q$ and $p=\infty$

nodes.name: Domination by $Mg$
nodes.statement: Appealing now to \eqref{gammak1t}, we deduce \begin{equation} \frac{1}{2^{k+1}}\int_{2^k}^{2^{k+1}}|g(x+\gamma(t))|dt \leq\frac{1}{2^{k+1}|\gamma'(2^k)|}\int_{-|\gamma(2^k)|-|\gamma(2^{k+1})|}^{|\gamma(2^k)|+|\gamma(2^{k+1})|}|g(x-u)|du \lesssim_{\gamma} Mg(x). \end{equation} Analogously, \begin{align*} \frac{1}{2^{k+1}}\int_{-2^{k+1}}^{-2^k}|g(x+\gamma(t))|dt&\lesssim_{\gamma} Mg(x). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Each dyadic average is $\lesssim Mg(x)$, on both sides of the origin.
nodes.section: 5.2 Bounds on the edge $(BC]$: $1< q\le \infty$, $r=q$ and $p=\infty$

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Therefore \begin{equation} \sup_{{j\in\mathbb{Z}}\atop{|j|>j_0}}\,\frac{1}{2^{j+1}}\int\limits_{2^j\le|t|\le2^{j+1}} |g(x+\gamma(t))|dt\lesssim_{\gamma} Mg(x). \end{equation} Using now the standard theory on Hardy Littlewood maximal operator we conclude our Theorem \ref{Mgamma}.
nodes.statement_short: Take the supremum and apply the Hardy-Littlewood maximal theorem.
nodes.section: 5.2 Bounds on the edge $(BC]$: $1< q\le \infty$, $r=q$ and $p=\infty$

nodes.name: Unboundedness of $M_\Gamma$ at the vertices $A$ and $B$
nodes.statement: In this section we show that our operator\footnote{Throughout this section we return to the original definition of our operator $M_\Gamma(f,g)$ in \eqref{definition}.} is unbounded at the points $\{A\}$ and $\{B\}$ (see Figure \ref{triangle_fig}).
nodes.section: 5.3 Behavior on $\{A\}\cup\{B\}$: triples $p=r=1,\, q=\infty$ and $p=\infty,\, q=r=1$
nodes.statement_short: $M_\Gamma$ fails to be bounded at $(p,q,r)=(1,\infty,1)$ and $(\infty,1,1)$.

nodes.name: Unboundedness at vertex $A$ ($p=r=1$, $q=\infty$)
nodes.statement: In this case, we show that there are functions $f\in L^1(\mathbb{R})$, $g\in L^\infty(\mathbb{R})$, and a map $\gamma\in\mathcal{NF}$ such that $M_\Gamma(f,g)$ is not bounded on $L^1$.
nodes.section: 5.3 Behavior on $\{A\}\cup\{B\}$: triples $p=r=1,\, q=\infty$ and $p=\infty,\, q=r=1$

nodes.name: Counterexample at vertex $A$
nodes.statement: Let $f=\chi_{[-1,1]}$ and $g=\chi_{(-\infty,1)}$ be characteristic functions, and let $\gamma(t)=t^2\in\mathcal{NF}$. Note that $f\in L^1(\mathbb{R})$, $g\in L^\infty(\mathbb{R})$ with $\|f\|_1=2$, and $\|g\|_\infty=1$. Then \begin{align*} M_\Gamma(f,g)(x)=\sup_{\varepsilon>0}\frac{1}{2\varepsilon}\int\limits_{-\varepsilon}^\varepsilon |f(x-t)g(x-t^2)|dt\ge \frac{1}{2(|x|+1)}\int\limits_{-(|x|+1)}^{|x|+1}f(x-t)g(x-t^2)dt. \end{align*} Suppose $x>2$, then \begin{align*} M_\Gamma(f,g)(x)\ge \frac{1}{2(x+1)}\int\limits_{x-1}^{x+1}f(x-t)g(x-t^2)dt=\frac{1}{2(x+1)}\int\limits_{x-1}^{x+1}g(x-t^2)dt\gtrsim\frac{1}{x+1}. \end{align*} Therefore, $M_\Gamma(f,g)$ is not absolutely integrable.
nodes.section: 5.3 Behavior on $\{A\}\cup\{B\}$: triples $p=r=1,\, q=\infty$ and $p=\infty,\, q=r=1$
nodes.statement_short: Construction: $f=\chi_{[-1,1]}$, $g=\chi_{(-\infty,1)}$, $\gamma(t)=t^2$ gives $M_\Gamma(f,g)(x)\gtrsim1/(x+1)$, not integrable.

nodes.name: Choice of $f,g,\gamma$
nodes.statement: Let $f=\chi_{[-1,1]}$ and $g=\chi_{(-\infty,1)}$ be characteristic functions, and let $\gamma(t)=t^2\in\mathcal{NF}$. Note that $f\in L^1(\mathbb{R})$, $g\in L^\infty(\mathbb{R})$ with $\|f\|_1=2$, and $\|g\|_\infty=1$.
nodes.section: 5.3 Behavior on $\{A\}\cup\{B\}$: triples $p=r=1,\, q=\infty$ and $p=\infty,\, q=r=1$

nodes.name: Lower bound by one scale
nodes.statement: Then \begin{align*} M_\Gamma(f,g)(x)=\sup_{\varepsilon>0}\frac{1}{2\varepsilon}\int\limits_{-\varepsilon}^\varepsilon |f(x-t)g(x-t^2)|dt\ge \frac{1}{2(|x|+1)}\int\limits_{-(|x|+1)}^{|x|+1}f(x-t)g(x-t^2)dt. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound $M_\Gamma$ below by the average at scale $|x|+1$.
nodes.section: 5.3 Behavior on $\{A\}\cup\{B\}$: triples $p=r=1,\, q=\infty$ and $p=\infty,\, q=r=1$

nodes.name: Decay $1/(x+1)$
nodes.statement: Suppose $x>2$, then \begin{align*} M_\Gamma(f,g)(x)\ge \frac{1}{2(x+1)}\int\limits_{x-1}^{x+1}f(x-t)g(x-t^2)dt=\frac{1}{2(x+1)}\int\limits_{x-1}^{x+1}g(x-t^2)dt\gtrsim\frac{1}{x+1}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: For $x>2$ the average is $\gtrsim1/(x+1)$.
nodes.section: 5.3 Behavior on $\{A\}\cup\{B\}$: triples $p=r=1,\, q=\infty$ and $p=\infty,\, q=r=1$

nodes.name: Not integrable
nodes.statement: Therefore, $M_\Gamma(f,g)$ is not absolutely integrable.
nodes.statement_short: Hence $M_\Gamma(f,g)\notin L^1$.
nodes.section: 5.3 Behavior on $\{A\}\cup\{B\}$: triples $p=r=1,\, q=\infty$ and $p=\infty,\, q=r=1$

nodes.name: Observation 5.4: weak-type bound at vertex $A$
nodes.statement: Notice that if $f\in L^1$ and $g\in L^\infty$ we have by \eqref{1inf1} \begin{align*} \{x\in\mathbb{R}:M_\Gamma(f,g)(x)>\alpha\}\subseteq \Big\{x\in\mathbb{R}:Mf(x)>\frac{\alpha}{\|g\|_\infty}\Big\}, \end{align*} for any $\alpha>0$. Thus, from the classical theory, we get that for any $\alpha>0$ the following holds: \begin{align*} |\{x\in\mathbb{R}:M_\Gamma(f,g)(x)>\alpha\}|\lesssim \frac{1}{\alpha}\|f\|_1 \|g\|_\infty\:. \end{align*}
nodes.section: 5.3 Behavior on $\{A\}\cup\{B\}$: triples $p=r=1,\, q=\infty$ and $p=\infty,\, q=r=1$
nodes.statement_short: At $A$, $M_\Gamma$ is still of weak type: $|\{M_\Gamma(f,g)>\alpha\}|\lesssim\alpha^{-1}\|f\|_1\|g\|_\infty$.

nodes.name: Unboundedness at vertex $B$ ($p=\infty$, $q=r=1$)
nodes.statement: We will show that there are functions $f\in L^\infty(\mathbb{R})$ and $g\in L^1(\mathbb{R})$ such that $M_\Gamma(f,g)$ is not bounded on $L^1$ for, say, $\gamma(t)=t^2$.
nodes.section: 5.3 Behavior on $\{A\}\cup\{B\}$: triples $p=r=1,\, q=\infty$ and $p=\infty,\, q=r=1$

nodes.name: Counterexample at vertex $B$
nodes.statement: Let $f$ be the constant function 1, and let $g=\chi_{[-1,1]}\in L^1(\mathbb{R})$. Then \begin{align*} M_\Gamma(f,g)(x)=\sup_{\varepsilon>0}\frac{1}{2\epsilon}\int_{-\varepsilon}^\varepsilon|g(x-t^2)|dt \simeq \sup_{\varepsilon>0}\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\int_\varepsilon^{2\varepsilon} |g(x-t^2)|dt. \end{align*} Notice that for any $\varepsilon>0$, we have \begin{align*} \frac{1}{\varepsilon}\int_\varepsilon^{2\varepsilon}|g(x-t^2)|dt=\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\int_{\varepsilon^2}^{4\varepsilon^2}\frac{|g(x-u)|}{2\sqrt{u}}du\ge \frac{1}{4\varepsilon^2}\int_{\varepsilon^2}^{4\varepsilon^2}|g(x-u)|du. \end{align*} Then, for $x>2$ we have \begin{align*} \frac{1}{\sqrt{(x+1)/4}} \int_{\sqrt{(x+1)/4}}^{2\,\sqrt{(x+1)/4}}|g(x-t^2)|dt\ge \frac{1}{x+1} \int\limits_{(x+1)/4}^{4(x+1)/4} |g(x-u)|du \gtrsim \frac{1}{x+1}. \end{align*} Therefore, $M(f,g) \not\in L^1(\mathbb{R})$.
nodes.section: 5.3 Behavior on $\{A\}\cup\{B\}$: triples $p=r=1,\, q=\infty$ and $p=\infty,\, q=r=1$
nodes.statement_short: Construction: $f\equiv1$, $g=\chi_{[-1,1]}$, $\gamma(t)=t^2$; substituting $u=t^2$ gives $M_\Gamma(f,g)(x)\gtrsim1/(x+1)$.

nodes.name: Choice of $f,g$
nodes.statement: Let $f$ be the constant function 1, and let $g=\chi_{[-1,1]}\in L^1(\mathbb{R})$. Then \begin{align*} M_\Gamma(f,g)(x)=\sup_{\varepsilon>0}\frac{1}{2\epsilon}\int_{-\varepsilon}^\varepsilon|g(x-t^2)|dt \simeq \sup_{\varepsilon>0}\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\int_\varepsilon^{2\varepsilon} |g(x-t^2)|dt. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Take $f\equiv1$, $g=\chi_{[-1,1]}$ and reduce to one-sided averages.
nodes.section: 5.3 Behavior on $\{A\}\cup\{B\}$: triples $p=r=1,\, q=\infty$ and $p=\infty,\, q=r=1$

nodes.name: Substitution $u=t^2$
nodes.statement: Notice that for any $\varepsilon>0$, we have \begin{align*} \frac{1}{\varepsilon}\int_\varepsilon^{2\varepsilon}|g(x-t^2)|dt=\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\int_{\varepsilon^2}^{4\varepsilon^2}\frac{|g(x-u)|}{2\sqrt{u}}du\ge \frac{1}{4\varepsilon^2}\int_{\varepsilon^2}^{4\varepsilon^2}|g(x-u)|du. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Substitute $u=t^2$ to compare with an average of $g$.
nodes.section: 5.3 Behavior on $\{A\}\cup\{B\}$: triples $p=r=1,\, q=\infty$ and $p=\infty,\, q=r=1$

nodes.name: Decay $1/(x+1)$
nodes.statement: Then, for $x>2$ we have \begin{align*} \frac{1}{\sqrt{(x+1)/4}} \int_{\sqrt{(x+1)/4}}^{2\,\sqrt{(x+1)/4}}|g(x-t^2)|dt\ge \frac{1}{x+1} \int\limits_{(x+1)/4}^{4(x+1)/4} |g(x-u)|du \gtrsim \frac{1}{x+1}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Choosing $\varepsilon=\sqrt{(x+1)/4}$ gives $\gtrsim1/(x+1)$.
nodes.section: 5.3 Behavior on $\{A\}\cup\{B\}$: triples $p=r=1,\, q=\infty$ and $p=\infty,\, q=r=1$

nodes.name: Not integrable
nodes.statement: Therefore, $M(f,g) \not\in L^1(\mathbb{R})$.
nodes.statement_short: Hence $M_\Gamma(f,g)\notin L^1$.
